papers.title_zh: IL-35 rs583911多态性与慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者肝癌风险的相关性
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background The immunoregulatory cytokine interleukin (IL)-35 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Here, we explored the association between single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the IL-35 gene and the occurrence of HCC in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV). Methods We selected 39 patients with chronic hepatitis B (HBV) and 52 patients with HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as the case groups, along with 42 healthy individuals as the control group. We genotyped five IL-35-related single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and analyzed their association with HCC risk. In addition, serum IL-35 levels, lymphocyte counts, and regulatory T cell (Treg) frequencies were measured in peripheral blood across all groups. Results The frequency of the rs583911 AA genotype tended to increase from healthy controls (4.8%) to patients with chronic HBV (10.3%) to patients with HCC (21.2%) (P for trend = 0.03). When patients with HCC were compared to non-HCC controls (healthy controls + chronic HBV carriers), the rs583911 AA genotype was associated with HCC risk (OR = 3.35; 95% CI: 1.17–9.61, P = 0.020). After adjusting for age, sex, cirrhosis status, and antiviral therapy, the association was no longer statistically significant (adjusted P = 0.085). Serum IL-35 levels were significantly elevated in both the HBV and the HCC groups compared with those in the control group ( P < 0.001), with no significant difference between the HBV and the HCC groups ( P = 0.434). Within the HCC subgroup, patients with the AA genotype tended to have higher IL-35 levels ( P = 0.047). Flow cytometry analysis of a subset of samples (6 controls, 6 patients with HBV, and 28 patients with HCC) revealed that the number of Treg cells was greater in patients with HCC than in those with HBV ( P = 0.038). Conclusion Our findings suggest a potential association between the rs583911 AA genotype and HBV-related HCC risk. However, these exploratory findings did not remain statistically significant after rigorous adjustment for multiple comparisons and potential confounders; therefore, validation in larger, independent cohorts is needed.

papers.title: Implementation gaps and policy priorities for viral hepatitis elimination in India
papers.abstract: Viral hepatitis remains a major public health challenge globally, with India bearing nearly 11.6% of the world’s chronic infections. To align with the World Health Organization’s target of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, India launched the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP), which employs virus-specific strategies including elimination of hepatitis C virus (HCV), reduction of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) burden, and strengthened prevention of enterically transmitted hepatitis. Through decentralization of services and provision of free generic direct-acting antivirals (DAAs), the programme has achieved substantial progress, with HCV cure rates exceeding 90% among treated individuals. Despite these gains, several implementation challenges continue to impede progress toward elimination targets. Critical gaps persist in the diagnostic cascade, including limited availability of integrated reflex viral load testing, inadequate access to HBV DNA testing, and the absence of routine hepatitis D virus (HDV) screening among HBsAg-positive individuals. Restrictive HBV treatment eligibility criteria, suboptimal hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine coverage, fragmented surveillance systems, and persistent stigma further undermine programme effectiveness. This persepective article examines the key barriers to viral hepatitis elimination in India and outlines priority policy actions. These include institutionalizing single-visit reflex molecular testing, expanding HBV treatment eligibility in accordance with the 2024 WHO guidelines, strengthening maternal antiviral prophylaxis and birth-dose vaccination strategies, improving outreach to marginalized populations, and integrating digital surveillance and patient-tracking systems to enhance continuity of care. Successful decentralized models, such as Punjab’s hepatitis programme, offer valuable lessons for scaling up effective interventions and accelerating India’s progress toward achieving its 2030 viral hepatitis elimination goals.erspective revi

papers.title_zh: 印度消除病毒性肝炎的实施差距和政策重点
papers.source_body_en: Viral hepatitis remains a major public health challenge globally, with India bearing nearly 11.6% of the world’s chronic infections. To align with the World Health Organization’s target of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, India launched the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP), which employs virus-specific strategies including elimination of hepatitis C virus (HCV), reduction of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) burden, and strengthened prevention of enterically transmitted hepatitis. Through decentralization of services and provision of free generic direct-acting antivirals (DAAs), the programme has achieved substantial progress, with HCV cure rates exceeding 90% among treated individuals. Despite these gains, several implementation challenges continue to impede progress toward elimination targets. Critical gaps persist in the diagnostic cascade, including limited availability of integrated reflex viral load testing, inadequate access to HBV DNA testing, and the absence of routine hepatitis D virus (HDV) screening among HBsAg-positive individuals. Restrictive HBV treatment eligibility criteria, suboptimal hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine coverage, fragmented surveillance systems, and persistent stigma further undermine programme effectiveness. This persepective article examines the key barriers to viral hepatitis elimination in India and outlines priority policy actions. These include institutionalizing single-visit reflex molecular testing, expanding HBV treatment eligibility in accordance with the 2024 WHO guidelines, strengthening maternal antiviral prophylaxis and birth-dose vaccination strategies, improving outreach to marginalized populations, and integrating digital surveillance and patient-tracking systems to enhance continuity of care. Successful decentralized models, such as Punjab’s hepatitis programme, offer valuable lessons for scaling up effective interventions and accelerating India’s progress toward achieving its 2030 viral hepatitis elimination goals.erspective revi

papers.title: Rare HBV Genotypes and Clinically Relevant Mutations of HBV and HCV During the COVID-19 Pandemic in a National Reference Outpatient Clinic in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B and C are major causes of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. The genetic diversity of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) influences disease progression, diagnosis, vaccine response, and antiviral treatment. Periods of healthcare disruption, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, reinforce the importance of molecular surveillance to monitor viral genotypes and clinically relevant mutations. This study described the distribution of HBV and HCV genotypes and mutations in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, during the COVID-19 pandemic. A cross-sectional study included 25 patients (15 HBV and 10 HCV) recruited between 2020 and 2022. Viral nucleic acids were amplified and sequenced by Sanger methodology, and mutations were analyzed using the Geno2pheno platform. HBV genotype A predominated (67%), comprising subgenotypes A1 (40%) and A2 (27%), followed by the rare genotypes B1 (13%), F2 (13%), and G (7%). Among HCV-infected individuals, genotypes 1a (40%) and 1b (30%) predominated, followed by genotypes 4 (20%) and 2 (10%). HBV immune escape mutations (Y100C and T126S) and unusual insertions in the S and RT domains were identified. In HCV, the substitutions C316Y, C316N, and S282R were detected. These findings highlight the importance of molecular surveillance for detecting clinically relevant viral variants.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma globally, and its genetic diversity affects disease progression, diagnosis, and treatment response. The study was motivated by the need to assess HBV genotype distribution and clinically relevant mutations during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period of healthcare disruption that may have impacted molecular surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in a national reference outpatient clinic in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, enrolling 25 patients (15 HBV and 10 HCV) between 2020 and 2022. Viral nucleic acids were amplified and sequenced using Sanger methodology, and mutations were analyzed with the Geno2pheno platform.
analysis.methods: The study focused on HBV and HCV genotypes and clinically relevant mutations.
analysis.main_results: HBV genotype A predominated (67%), comprising subgenotypes A1 (40%) and A2 (27%), followed by rare genotypes B1 (13%), F2 (13%), and G (7%). HBV immune escape mutations (Y100C and T126S) and unusual insertions in the S and RT domains were identified.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight the detection of rare HBV genotypes and clinically relevant mutations, underscoring the importance of molecular surveillance during periods of healthcare disruption. The identification of immune escape mutations and unusual insertions represents a novel contribution to local HBV molecular epidemiology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the need for ongoing molecular surveillance of HBV to inform diagnosis, vaccine strategies, and antiviral treatment decisions, particularly in settings with limited prior genotype data.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=15 HBV cases) and single-center design limit generalizability and statistical power. The evidence strength is moderate due to the descriptive nature of the study and absence of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from a national reference clinic in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, assessed HBV and HCV genotypes and clinically relevant mutations during 2020–2022. Among 15 HBV-infected patients, genotype A predominated (67%), including rare subgenotypes B1, F2, and G, alongside immune escape mutations (Y100C, T126S) and unusual insertions in S and RT domains. The study underscores the value of molecular surveillance during pandemic-era healthcare disruptions for informing diagnosis and treatment strategies. Limitations include a small sample size and single-center design, yielding moderate-strength evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 仍然是全球肝硬化和肝细胞癌的主要原因,其遗传多样性影响疾病进展、诊断 和 治疗 反应。这项研究的动机是需要评估 COVID-19 大流行期间的 HBV 基因型分布和临床相关的 突变,这段医疗保健中断的时期可能会影响分子 监测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项横断面研究在巴西里约热内卢的国家参考门诊诊所进行,2020年至2022年间招募了25名患者(15名乙肝患者和10名丙肝患者)。使用Sanger方法对病毒核酸进行扩增和测序,并使用Geno2pheno平台对突变进行分析。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究重点关注 HBV 和 HCV 基因型以及临床相关的 突变。
elements_zh.main_results: HBV 基因型 A 占主导地位 (67%),包括亚基因型 A1 (40%) 和 A2 (27%),其次是罕见基因型 B1 (13%)、F2 (13%) 和 G (7%)。鉴定出 HBV 免疫逃逸 突变(Y100C 和 T126S)以及 S 和 RT 结构域中的异常插入。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者强调了罕见 HBV 基因型和临床相关 监测 的检测,强调了分子 监测 在医疗保健中断期间的重要性。免疫逃逸 突变 和异常插入的鉴定代表了对局部 HBV 分子 流行病学 的新贡献。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持需要持续进行 HBV 分子 监测 来为 诊断、疫苗 策略和 抗病毒药物 治疗 决策提供信息,特别是在先前基因型数据有限的情况下。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 小样本量(n = 15 HBV 病例)和单中心设计限制了普遍性和统计功效。由于研究的描述性和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 巴西里约热内卢国家参考门诊诊所在 COVID-19 大流行期间罕见的 HBV 基因型以及 HBV 和 HCV 的临床相关 突变
papers.source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B and C are major causes of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. The genetic diversity of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) influences disease progression, diagnosis, vaccine response, and antiviral treatment. Periods of healthcare disruption, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, reinforce the importance of molecular surveillance to monitor viral genotypes and clinically relevant mutations. This study described the distribution of HBV and HCV genotypes and mutations in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, during the COVID-19 pandemic. A cross-sectional study included 25 patients (15 HBV and 10 HCV) recruited between 2020 and 2022. Viral nucleic acids were amplified and sequenced by Sanger methodology, and mutations were analyzed using the Geno2pheno platform. HBV genotype A predominated (67%), comprising subgenotypes A1 (40%) and A2 (27%), followed by the rare genotypes B1 (13%), F2 (13%), and G (7%). Among HCV-infected individuals, genotypes 1a (40%) and 1b (30%) predominated, followed by genotypes 4 (20%) and 2 (10%). HBV immune escape mutations (Y100C and T126S) and unusual insertions in the S and RT domains were identified. In HCV, the substitutions C316Y, C316N, and S282R were detected. These findings highlight the importance of molecular surveillance for detecting clinically relevant viral variants.

papers.title: Post-vaccination hepatitis B seroprotection among kidney transplant recipients in Saudi Arabia: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background: Evidence regarding post-vaccination hepatitis B virus (HBV) seroprotection among kidney transplant recipients in Saudi Arabia remains limited. This study estimated the prevalence of seroprotection and evaluated factors associated with vaccine nonresponse. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients followed at Prince Sultan Military Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, who had documented hepatitis B vaccination and subsequent quantitative measurement of antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs). Seroprotection was defined as an anti-HBs concentration of at least 10 mIU/ml. Participant characteristics were compared according to seroprotection status. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between non-seroprotection and total number of hepatitis B vaccine doses. Results: Among 100 kidney transplant recipients, the mean (SD) age was 41.4 (15.2) years, and 66 participants (66.0%) were male. Overall, 69 recipients achieved seroprotection (69.0%; 95% CI, 59.4-77.2%), whereas 31 (31.0%) remained non-seroprotected. Vaccine dose category differed significantly by seroprotection status (p=0.014); 80.6% of non-seroprotected recipients had received only 1 to 2 doses compared with 50.7% of seroprotected recipients. In the adjusted model, no variable was independently associated with non-seroprotection. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with higher, but not statistically significant, odds of non-seroprotection (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 0.96-2.16; p=0.079). Conclusions: Nearly one-third of vaccinated kidney transplant recipients lacked serological protection against HBV. Routine post-vaccination anti-HBs testing and individualized booster or revaccination strategies should be considered, particularly for older recipients and those who have received fewer vaccine doses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Evidence regarding post-vaccination hepatitis B virus (HBV) seroprotection among kidney transplant recipients in Saudi Arabia remains limited, prompting the need to estimate seroprotection prevalence and identify factors associated with vaccine nonresponse.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 100 adult kidney transplant recipients followed at Prince Sultan Military Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, who had documented hepatitis B vaccination and subsequent quantitative measurement of antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs).
analysis.methods: Seroprotection was defined as an anti-HBs concentration of at least 10 mIU/ml, participant characteristics were compared by seroprotection status, and multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations between non-seroprotection and total number of hepatitis B vaccine doses.
analysis.main_results: Among 100 recipients, 69 achieved seroprotection (69.0%; 95% CI, 59.4-77.2%), while 31 remained non-seroprotected; vaccine dose category differed significantly by seroprotection status (p=0.014), with 80.6% of non-seroprotected recipients having received only 1 to 2 doses versus 50.7% of seroprotected recipients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that nearly one-third of vaccinated kidney transplant recipients lacked serological protection against HBV, highlighting the need for routine post-vaccination anti-HBs testing and individualized booster or revaccination strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that routine post-vaccination anti-HBs testing and individualized booster or revaccination strategies should be considered, particularly for older recipients and those who have received fewer vaccine doses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center retrospective design and lack of independent associations in adjusted models limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study from Saudi Arabia assessed post-vaccination hepatitis B virus (HBV) seroprotection among 100 adult kidney transplant recipients. It found that 69% achieved seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/ml), while 31% remained non-seroprotected. Vaccine dose category differed significantly by seroprotection status, with fewer doses associated with non-seroprotection. No variables were independently associated with non-seroprotection in adjusted models, though older age showed a non-significant trend toward higher odds. The authors recommend routine post-vaccination anti-HBs testing and individualized booster or revaccination strategies, particularly for older recipients and those with fewer vaccine doses. The single-center retrospective design and absence of independent associations limit causal inference and generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 关于沙特阿拉伯肾移植受者 疫苗接种 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 血清保护作用的证据仍然有限,提示需要估计 患病率 血清保护作用并确定与 疫苗 无反应相关的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项单中心回顾性 队列研究 研究纳入了沙特阿拉伯利雅得苏丹王子军事医学城的 100 名成年肾移植受者,他们记录了乙型肝炎 队列研究 以及随后对乙型肝炎表面抗原(抗 HBs)抗体的定量测量。
elements_zh.methods: 血清保护被定义为抗-HBs浓度至少为10 mIU/ml,通过血清保护状态比较参与者特征,多变量逻辑回归评估非血清保护与乙型肝炎疫苗剂量总数之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 在100名受者中,69名达到血清保护(69.0%;95%置信区间,59.4-77.2%),而31名未达到血清保护;疫苗剂次类别在血清保护状态上存在显著差异(p=0.014),其中未达到血清保护的受者中有80.6%仅接种1至2剂,而达到血清保护的受者中有50.7%接种1至2剂。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为,近三分之一的肾移植受者缺乏针对 HBV 的血清学保护,这凸显了 疫苗接种 后常规抗 HBs 检测和个体化加强疫苗或重新疫苗接种策略的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,应考虑常规 疫苗接种 后抗 HBs 检测和个体化加强免疫或重新接种策略,特别是对于老年受者和接受较少 疫苗 剂量的人。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单中心回顾性设计和调整模型中缺乏独立关联限制了因果推断和普遍性,需要中等强度的证据。

papers.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯肾移植受者 疫苗接种 后乙型肝炎血清保护:一项回顾性 队列研究 研究
papers.source_body_en: Background: Evidence regarding post-vaccination hepatitis B virus (HBV) seroprotection among kidney transplant recipients in Saudi Arabia remains limited. This study estimated the prevalence of seroprotection and evaluated factors associated with vaccine nonresponse. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients followed at Prince Sultan Military Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, who had documented hepatitis B vaccination and subsequent quantitative measurement of antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs). Seroprotection was defined as an anti-HBs concentration of at least 10 mIU/ml. Participant characteristics were compared according to seroprotection status. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between non-seroprotection and total number of hepatitis B vaccine doses. Results: Among 100 kidney transplant recipients, the mean (SD) age was 41.4 (15.2) years, and 66 participants (66.0%) were male. Overall, 69 recipients achieved seroprotection (69.0%; 95% CI, 59.4-77.2%), whereas 31 (31.0%) remained non-seroprotected. Vaccine dose category differed significantly by seroprotection status (p=0.014); 80.6% of non-seroprotected recipients had received only 1 to 2 doses compared with 50.7% of seroprotected recipients. In the adjusted model, no variable was independently associated with non-seroprotection. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with higher, but not statistically significant, odds of non-seroprotection (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 0.96-2.16; p=0.079). Conclusions: Nearly one-third of vaccinated kidney transplant recipients lacked serological protection against HBV. Routine post-vaccination anti-HBs testing and individualized booster or revaccination strategies should be considered, particularly for older recipients and those who have received fewer vaccine doses.

analysis_zh.main_results: 在100名受者中,69名达到血清保护(69.0%;95%置信区间,59.4-77.2%),而31名未达到血清保护;疫苗剂次类别在血清保护状态上存在显著差异(p=0.014),其中未达到血清保护的受者中有80.6%仅接种1至2剂,而达到血清保护的受者中有50.7%接种1至2剂。

papers.title: Revisiting the Gray Zone in HBeAg-Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Insights From a Multicenter Liver Biopsy Cohort
papers.abstract: Background/Aims: The management of patients with HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB) with intermediate viremia and persistently normal alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels remains controversial. This “gray-zone” (GZ) population may harbor significant histological liver injury despite not meeting conventional treatment criteria. This study characterized the histologic features of this GZ population and compared their clinical and laboratory characteristics. Materials and Methods: In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with HBeAg negative CHB who had hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels between 2000 and 20 000 IU/mL and persistently normal ALT levels and who underwent liver biopsy between 2014 and 2022 were included. Histological assessment was performed using the modified Ishak scoring system. Significant fibrosis was defined as Ishak stage of 2 or greater. Clinical, virological, and noninvasive fibrosis parameters were analyzed. Results: A total of 145 patients were included (mean age: 46.3 ± 12.6 years; 54.5% female). Significant fibrosis and/or moderate-tosevere necroinflammatory activity requiring antiviral therapy was identified in 109 patients (75.1%). Although ALT and aspartate aminotransferase levels remained within normal reference range, both were significantly higher in the treatment group compared than in the nontreatment group (P = .003 and P = .018, respectively). Aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ration index (APRI) scores were also significantly elevated among treated patients (P = .02), whereas Fibrorsis-4 (FIB-4) scores did not differ significantly. HBV DNA and quantitative Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels were comparable between groups. Conclusion: A substantial proportion of patients with HBeAg-negative CHB in the GZ exhibited clinically significant histologic disease despite persistently normal ALT levels. Reliance solely on conventional biochemical thresholds may underestimate the burden of fibrosis. Early histological evaluation and more proactive treatment strategies should be considered for selected patients in the GZ. Cite this article as: Gül Ö, Köseoğlu H, Yalçın S, et al. Revisiting the gray zone in HBeAg negative chronic hepatitis B: Insights from a multicenter liver biopsy cohort. Turk J Gastroenterol. Published online August 11, 2026. doi: 10.5152/tjg.2026.26367.

papers.source_body_en: Background/Aims: The management of patients with HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB) with intermediate viremia and persistently normal alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels remains controversial. Materials and Methods: In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with HBeAg negative CHB who had hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels between 2000 and 20 000 IU/mL and persistently normal ALT levels and who underwent liver biopsy between 2014 and 2022 were included. Histological assessment was performed using the modified Ishak scoring system. Significant fibrosis was defined as Ishak stage of 2 or greater. Clinical, virological, and noninvasive fibrosis parameters were analyzed. Results: A total of 145 patients were included (mean age: 46.3 ± 12.6 years; 54.5% female). Reliance solely on conventional biochemical thresholds may underestimate the burden of fibrosis. papers.title: Quantitative HBsAg as a biomarker for disease staging in untreated chronic hepatitis B patients: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background and aims Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major issue in North Africa, where HBeAg-negative profiles are predominant. Distinguishing between chronic infection and active chronic hepatitis using conventional markers is sometimes difficult. Our study assessed the correlation of HBsAg with viral load and liver fibrosis, as well as its performance in distinguishing the different evolving phases of chronic HBV infection. Approach and results We conducted an analytical cross-sectional study that included 90 HBeAg-negative treatment-naïve patients. All patients underwent biological assessment, HBsAg quantification, viral load, and FibroScan®. Among the 90 patients (mean age: 47.5 ± 11 years; 52.6% women), 65.6% were in the low-replicative chronic infection phase. The median viral load was 328.5 IU/mL, and the median HBsAg level was 213.5 IU/mL. A strong positive correlation was observed between HBsAg and HBV DNA levels ( r = 0.721, p < 0.001). HBsAg levels showed a weak but significant association with liver fibrosis ( p = 0.007, AUC = 0.631). The performance of HBsAg in differentiating low versus high replicative phases was excellent (AUC = 0.819; p < 0.001), with an optimal threshold of 450 IU/mL (sensitivity: 81.3%; specificity: 77.6%). In multivariate analysis, HBV DNA and AST were independently associated with disease phase, whereas qHBsAg was not an independent predictor. Conclusion Quantitative HBsAg measurement is a relevant tool for refining the stratification of untreated HBeAg-negative patients as a complementary surrogate marker. When combined with viral load, transaminases, and FibroScan®, HBsAg could contribute to optimized monitoring and better resource allocation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection poses a significant public-health burden in North Africa where HBeAg-negative profiles predominate, and conventional markers sometimes fail to distinguish chronic infection from active chronic hepatitis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An analytical cross-sectional study enrolled 90 HBeAg-negative, treatment-naïve patients (mean age 47.5 ± 11 years; 52.6% women) and performed biological assessment, HBsAg quantification, viral load measurement, and FibroScan®.
analysis.methods: HBsAg and HBV DNA were quantified, and liver fibrosis was assessed by FibroScan®; correlation and diagnostic performance were evaluated using statistical tests and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
analysis.main_results: HBsAg showed a strong positive correlation with HBV DNA (r = 0.721, p < 0.001), a weak but significant association with liver fibrosis (p = 0.007, AUC = 0.631), and excellent performance in differentiating low- versus high-replicative phases (AUC = 0.819, p < 0.001) with an optimal threshold of 450 IU/mL (sensitivity 81.3%, specificity 77.6%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret quantitative HBsAg as a relevant complementary surrogate marker for refining stratification of untreated HBeAg-negative chronic HBV patients, highlighting its added value when combined with viral load, transaminases, and FibroScan®.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that HBsAg quantification could improve monitoring strategies and resource allocation in chronic HBV infection management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and single-centre setting limit causal inference and generalisability, warranting prospective validation; overall evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in 90 HBeAg-negative, treatment-naïve chronic HBV patients assessed quantitative HBsAg as a biomarker for disease staging. HBsAg correlated strongly with HBV DNA (r = 0.721, p < 0.001) and weakly with liver fibrosis (AUC = 0.631), while showing excellent discrimination between low- and high-replicative phases (AUC = 0.819) at a threshold of 450 IU/mL (sensitivity 81.3%, specificity 77.6%). Multivariate analysis indicated HBV DNA and AST, but not HBsAg, were independent predictors of disease phase. The authors conclude that quantitative HBsAg is a relevant complementary tool for stratifying untreated HBeAg-negative patients, potentially improving monitoring and resource allocation when combined with viral load, transaminases, and FibroScan®. The single-centre, cross-sectional design limits causal inference and generalisability, yielding moderate-strength evidence.

papers.title: The Impact of Chronic Hepatitis D Virus Infection on Health-Related Quality of Life and Fatigue: A Real-World International Study.
papers.abstract: As little is known about the disease burden of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection, this study examined health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue at different disease stages. This was a real-world quantitative cross-sectional survey of patients in Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA. Patients were recruited via their treating physicians. Patients who had received bulevirtide for hepatitis B or treatment licensed for HDV were excluded. Of 211 patients, 41% were noncirrhotic (F0-F3); 20% had liver cirrhosis with normal function (compensated); 20% had liver cirrhosis (F4) with impaired function (decompensated); 19% had hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Mean (standard deviation; SD) age was 54.5 (11.5) years, 75% were male. ANOVA showed a significant decrease (indicating poorer HRQoL) in EQ-5D-3L visual analogue scale (VAS) scores and index values with worsening disease stage and increasing severity (all p < 0.0001). All domain scores of the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 (except positive wellbeing) worsened with progressing disease and increasing symptom severity (all p ≤ 0.0001). Mean Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) total scores also increased, indicating greater fatigue, with worsening of disease and increasing symptom severity (both p < 0.0001). HDV infection significantly impacts patients' HRQoL and fatigue, particularly for patients at later disease stages. Treatments that slow disease progression, reducing the burden of HDV infection, are needed.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection imposes a poorly understood disease burden, prompting this study to quantify its impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue across disease stages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This real-world cross-sectional survey enrolled patients from Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA via treating physicians, excluding those treated with bulevirtide for hepatitis B or HDV-specific therapy.
analysis.methods: The study assessed HRQoL using EQ-5D-3L visual analogue scale and index values and the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2, and measured fatigue with the Fatigue Severity Scale, comparing outcomes by disease stage.
analysis.main_results: ANOVA revealed significantly lower EQ-5D-3L scores and index values with worsening disease stage (all p < 0.0001), and all Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 domain scores except positive wellbeing declined with increasing severity (all p ≤ 0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that HDV infection substantially impairs HRQoL and increases fatigue, particularly in advanced disease stages, highlighting an unmet need for therapies that slow progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the importance of early detection and intervention to mitigate HRQoL deterioration and fatigue in HDV-infected patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and exclusion of treated patients limit causal inference and generalisability, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This real-world cross-sectional study across Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA examined the impact of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue. Patients were recruited via physicians and stratified by disease stage, excluding those receiving bulevirtide or HDV-specific therapy. Using EQ-5D-3L and the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2, the authors observed significant declines in HRQoL with worsening disease stage (all p < 0.0001), while the Fatigue Severity Scale showed increased fatigue severity (p < 0.0001). The study concludes that HDV infection substantially impairs HRQoL and increases fatigue, particularly in advanced stages, and calls for treatments that slow disease progression. The cross-sectional design and exclusion of treated patients limit causal inference and generalisability, resulting in moderate confidence.

papers.title: Tenofovir Alafenamide Versus Entecavir as Switch Therapy After Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate in Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Background: Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) and entecavir (ETV) are recommended alternatives to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) for patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) at increased risk of kidney injury. However, data from direct head-to-head comparisons of their long-term renal safety and antiviral efficacy after switching from TDF are lacking. We aimed to compare these outcomes between TAF and ETV. Methods: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included consecutive CHB patients who switched from TDF to either TAF or ETV between January 2012 and December 2021. Inverse probability of treatment weighting using the propensity score was applied to balance the baseline characteristics. Changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were assessed using a linear mixed-effects model. Renal dysfunction was defined as a decline of at least one GFR category. Results: A total of 235 patients were included (TAF, n = 168; ETV, n = 67). After adjustment for key risk factors, the mean eGFR decline over 36 months was not significantly different between the TAF and ETV groups (−3.21 mL/min/1.73 m2 [95% CI, −4.98 to −1.44] vs. −3.49 mL/min/1.73 m2 [95% CI, −9.49 to −2.50]; p = 0.856). The 3-year cumulative incidence of renal dysfunction was also not significantly different between groups (16.6% [95% CI, 10.5–23.3] vs. 7.8% [95% CI, 2.7–16.2]; p = 0.135). Alanine aminotransferase normalization rates (83.0% vs. 78.8%; p = 0.575) and virological suppression rates (97.8% vs. 97.1%; p = 1.000) were similarly high in both groups. Conclusions: TAF and ETV demonstrated similar long-term renal safety and antiviral efficacy, supporting both agents as reasonable switch options for CHB patients requiring TDF discontinuation because of renal safety concerns.

papers.title: Knowledge of Hepatitis B Infection Vaccination Status, Risk Perception and Barriers among Hospital Cleaners at the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital Gwagwalada, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hospital cleaners occupy a frontline position in healthcare infection control, yet remain among the least studied occupational groups in hepatitis B research. This study assessed knowledge of hepatitis B infection and its vaccine, risk perception, vaccination status, and barriers to vaccination among cleaners at the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital (UATH), Gwagwalada, Nigeria. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 145 cleaners selected by systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, hepatitis B knowledge, risk perception, vaccination status, and barriers to vaccination. Analysis was performed with SPSS version 23, using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Ethical approval was obtained from the Health Research Ethics Committee of UATH. Results All 145 questionnaires were returned (response rate 100%). Mean age was 40.63 ± 9.96 years; 73.1% were female. Knowledge of hepatitis B was good in 135 participants (93.1%), and knowledge of the hepatitis B vaccine was good in 111 (76.6%). Good risk perception was recorded in 106 participants (73.1%). Despite this, only 49 cleaners (33.8%) had received at least one vaccine dose, and only 19 (13.1%) had completed the full three-dose series. Among those incompletely or unvaccinated, lack of awareness (66.2%), absence of an appropriate hospital vaccination policy (57.9%), inadequate orientation for new staff (53.8%), and unaffordability (37.2%) were the principal barriers identified. Years of work experience (p = 0.005) and age (p = 0.023) were significantly associated with vaccination status. Conclusion Despite generally adequate knowledge and risk awareness, hepatitis B vaccination coverage among hospital cleaners at UATH remains critically low. Systemic institutional shortcomings, particularly the absence of enforceable vaccination policies and structured orientation programs, are more proximate barriers than individual knowledge gaps. Targeted policy reform and workplace vaccination programs are urgently needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the knowledge, risk perception, vaccination status, and barriers to vaccination against hepatitis B among hospital cleaners at the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital, Gwagwalada, Nigeria. A descriptive cross-sectional design was used, with 145 cleaners surveyed via a structured questionnaire. The results showed that while knowledge of hepatitis B and its vaccine was generally good, vaccination coverage was critically low, with only 13.1% completing the full three-dose series. Factors such as years of work experience and age were significantly associated with vaccination status. The authors emphasize that institutional shortcomings, rather than individual knowledge gaps, are the primary barriers to vaccination. These findings highlight the need for policy reform and workplace vaccination programs to improve hepatitis B prevention among this occupational group. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the abstract-only nature of the analysis and potential self-reporting bias.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估尼日利亚瓜瓦拉达阿布贾大学教学医院的医院清洁工对乙型肝炎感染及其 疫苗 的了解、风险认知、疫苗接种 状态以及 疫苗接种 的障碍。医院清洁工在医疗保健感染控制中处于前线地位,但仍然是乙型肝炎研究中研究最少的职业群体之一。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对尼日利亚瓜瓦拉达阿布贾大学教学医院通过系统随机抽样选出的 145 名清洁工进行了一项描述性横断面研究。共收回 145 份问卷,平均年龄为 40.63 ± 9.96 岁,其中 73.1% 为女性。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化、访谈员管理的问卷收集数据,涵盖社会人口学特征、乙型肝炎知识、风险认知、疫苗接种 状态以及 疫苗接种 障碍。使用 SPSS 23 版进行分析,使用描述性统计和卡方检验。
elements_zh.main_results: 135 名参与者 (93.1%) 的乙型肝炎知识良好,111 名参与者 (76.6%) 的乙型肝炎 疫苗 知识良好。106 名参与者 (73.1%) 具有良好的风险认知。尽管如此,只有 49 名清洁工 (33.8%) 至少接受了一剂 疫苗,并且只有 19 名 (13.1%) 完成了完整的三剂系列。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 工作经验年数 (p = 0.005) 和年龄 (p = 0.023) 与 疫苗接种 状态显着相关。该研究强调需要进行有针对性的政策改革和工作场所 疫苗接种 计划,以提高乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 的覆盖率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了解决系统性制度缺陷的重要性,例如缺乏可执行的 疫苗接种 政策和结构化的定向计划,以加强医院清洁工的乙型肝炎预防工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象分析,由于缺乏详细的统计分析以及基于问卷的数据可能存在自我报告偏差,因此证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 医院清洁工在医疗保健感染控制中处于前线地位,但仍然是乙型肝炎研究中研究最少的职业群体之一。本研究评估了尼日利亚瓜瓦拉达阿布贾大学教学医院 (UATH) 清洁工对乙型肝炎感染及其 疫苗 的了解、风险认知、疫苗接种 状况以及 疫苗接种 的障碍。方法对通过系统随机抽样抽取的145名清洁工进行描述性横断面研究。使用结构化、访谈员管理的问卷收集数据,涵盖社会人口学特征、乙型肝炎知识、风险认知、疫苗接种 状态以及 疫苗接种 障碍。使用 SPSS 23 版进行分析,使用描述性统计和卡方检验。获得了 UATH 健康研究伦理委员会的伦理批准。结果 145份问卷全部收回(有效率为100%)。平均年龄为 40.63 ± 9.96 岁;73.1%为女性。135 名参与者 (93.1%) 的乙型肝炎知识良好,111 名参与者 (76.6%) 的乙型肝炎 疫苗 知识良好。106 名参与者 (73.1%) 具有良好的风险认知。尽管如此,只有 49 名清洁工 (33.8%) 至少接受了一剂 疫苗,并且只有 19 名 (13.1%) 完成了完整的三剂系列。在那些不完全或未接种疫苗的人中,缺乏认识(66.2%)、缺乏适当的医院 疫苗接种 政策(57.9%)、新员工培训不足(53.8%)和负担不起(37.2%)是确定的主要障碍。工作经验年数 (p = 0.005) 和年龄 (p = 0.023) 与 疫苗接种 状态显着相关。结论 尽管普遍具备足够的知识和风险意识,UATH 医院清洁工的乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 覆盖率仍然极低。系统性制度缺陷,特别是缺乏可执行的 疫苗接种 政策和结构化的定向计划,是比个人知识差距更直接的障碍。迫切需要有针对性的政策改革和工作场所 疫苗接种 计划。

papers.title: Determinants of Hepatitis B Vaccination Uptake and Hepatitis B and C Preventive Practices Among Healthcare Workers in Tertiary Health Institutions in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study determined the determinants of Hepatitis B vaccination uptake and Hepatitis B and C preventive practices among healthcare workers in tertiary health institutions in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, Nigeria.  Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study design, mixed methods was adopted. A multi-stage sampling technique was used to recruit 385 healthcare workers from selected tertiary health institutions in the FCT. Data were collected using a pre-tested, self-administered, structured questionnaire. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS version 25.0. Frequencies and proportions were computed for categorical variables.
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

papers.title: A First-in-Human study of AHB-137, an unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide, in healthy subjects and patients with chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: AHB-137 is a novel ASO targeting a conserved region near the 3′ end of all HBV mRNA. This first-in-human phase 1 study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and antiviral efficacy in healthy subjects and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. Methods: Forty healthy subjects were randomized into four placebo-controlled single ascending dose (100-450 mg, 6:2 AHB-137:placebo) cohorts and one multiple-dose (MD; 300 mg, 6:2) cohort receiving four weekly subcutaneous doses with a Day 4 loading dose (5 doses). Twenty-four virally suppressed, HBeAg-negative CHB patients on stable nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy were enrolled: four in an open-label 300-mg MD cohort (5 doses) and 20 in two placebo-controlled 300-mg MD cohorts (4:1, stratified by baseline HBsAg), receiving an additional loading dose on Day 11 (6 doses). Results: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 73% of healthy subjects and 71% of CHB patients and were primarily mild or moderate injection-site reactions and headaches. No treatment-related serious adverse events, discontinuations, or deaths were observed. PK profiles showed rapid absorption (T max 2.96-5.50 h), dose-proportional exposure, no significant accumulation, long terminal half-life (150-220 h), and minimal renal excretion. In CHB patients, AHB-137 treatment led to a rapid HBsAg decline (mean 0.7-1.0 log 10 IU/mL). HBsAg loss ( Conclusions: In this Phase 1 study, AHB-137 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, predictable PK, and rapid and prolonged HBsAg reductions, supporting further evaluation of dosing and treatment duration in CHB.

papers.source_body_en: Background & Aims: AHB-137 is a novel ASO targeting a conserved region near the 3′ end of all HBV mRNA. In CHB patients, AHB-137 treatment led to a rapid HBsAg decline (mean 0.7-1.0 log 10 IU/mL). HBsAg loss ( Conclusions: In this Phase 1 study, AHB-137 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, predictable PK, and rapid and prolonged HBsAg reductions, supporting further evaluation of dosing and treatment duration in CHB.

papers.title: Peripheral Blood Immunogenomic Cytokine-receptor Signature (CXCR1, IL11RA, IL13RA2, CD19) Predicts HBV-related Cirrhosis: Public PBMC Transcriptome Mining and Nomogram Development
papers.abstract: Progression from chronic hepatitis B (CHB) to cirrhosis is closely associated with immune dysregulation and altered cytokine signaling, yet effective noninvasive immune biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to develop a peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC)-based cytokine gene signature for predicting HBV-related cirrhosis. The GSE114783 microarray dataset was analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes between CHB and cirrhosis. Immune-related candidate genes were selected by integrating curated immune resources and the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction pathway. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression were used to construct the predictive model. Receiver operating characteristic analysis, leave-one-out cross-validation, and nomogram development were performed to evaluate model performance and support clinical translation. Differential expression analysis identified 3169 genes distinguishing cirrhosis from CHB, from which 86 immune/cytokine-related genes were prioritized. LASSO selected a parsimonious 4-gene signature-CXCR1, IL11RA, IL13RA2, and CD19-capturing key immune axes relevant to chronic inflammation and fibrogenesis (chemokine receptor signaling, IL-11/IL-13 receptor pathways, and B-cell–associated immunity). The resulting model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.935 (95% CI, 0.882-0.988); at an optimal cutoff of 0.832, sensitivity was 88.6% and specificity 84.3%. LOOCV supported robust performance, and the nomogram demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risk. A PBMC-based immune cytokine-receptor gene signature (CXCR1/IL11RA/IL13RA2/CD19) provides a noninvasive tool for immunologically informed risk stratification of HBV-related cirrhosis and may support immune monitoring and early intervention strategies. Prospective, multicohort validation and mechanistic studies are warranted.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 进展为肝硬化与免疫失调和细胞因子信号传导改变有关,但用于风险分层的非侵入性免疫生物标志物仍然很少。该研究通过寻找基于外周血单核细胞 (PBMC) 的细胞因子基因特征来预测 HBV 相关肝硬化,从而弥补了知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 GSE114783 微阵列数据集,以确定 CHB 和 HBV 相关肝硬化之间的差异表达基因。它使用免疫相关候选基因选择,整合策划的免疫资源和 KEGG 细胞因子-细胞因子受体相互作用途径。
elements_zh.methods: 差异表达分析确定了 3169 个区分肝硬化和 CHB 的基因,其中优先考虑了 86 个免疫/细胞因子相关基因。使用 LASSO 回归和多变量逻辑回归构建预测模型,然后进行接受者操作特征分析、留一法交叉验证和列线图开发来评估性能。
elements_zh.main_results: 所构建的模型达到的曲线下面积(AUC)为0.935(95%置信区间,0.882-0.988);在最优截点0.832时,敏感性为88.6%,特异性为84.3%。留一法交叉验证支持模型性能稳健,且列线图显示预测风险与观察风险间具有良好的一致性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 4 基因特征(CXCR1、IL11RA、IL13RA2、CD19)解释为捕获与慢性炎症和纤维发生相关的关键免疫轴,代表了一种用于对 HBV 相关肝硬化进行免疫学知情风险分层的无创工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 基于 PBMC 的免疫细胞因子受体基因特征可能支持 HBV 相关肝硬化的免疫监测和早期干预策略,为临床实践中的风险分层提供无创方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖单一公共数据集且缺乏前瞻性、多队列验证而受到限制,需要进一步研究以确认普遍性和临床实用性。

analysis_zh.methods: 差异表达分析确定了 3169 个区分肝硬化和 CHB 的基因,其中优先考虑了 86 个免疫/细胞因子相关基因。使用 LASSO 回归和多变量逻辑回归构建预测模型,然后进行接受者操作特征分析、留一法交叉验证和列线图开发来评估性能。
analysis_zh.main_results: 所构建的模型达到的曲线下面积(AUC)为0.935(95%置信区间,0.882-0.988);在最优截点0.832时,敏感性为88.6%,特异性为84.3%。留一法交叉验证支持模型性能稳健,且列线图显示预测风险与观察风险间具有良好的一致性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 4 基因特征(CXCR1、IL11RA、IL13RA2、CD19)解释为捕获与慢性炎症和纤维发生相关的关键免疫轴,代表了一种用于对 HBV 相关肝硬化进行免疫学知情风险分层的无创工具。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 基于 PBMC 的免疫细胞因子受体基因特征可能支持 HBV 相关肝硬化的免疫监测和早期干预策略,为临床实践中的风险分层提供无创方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖单一公共数据集且缺乏前瞻性、多队列验证而受到限制,需要进一步研究以确认普遍性和临床实用性。

papers.full_text: Abstract Hepatitis B virus, a pararetrovirus and member of hepadnaviridae family, harbours a partially double-stranded DNA genome that is transcribed by the host RNA polymerase II to generate an intron-containing pregenomic RNA (pgRNA). Nuclear export of pgRNA utilizing the canonical host pathways remains central to successful virus replication since it is reverse transcribed by the viral P protein within the nucleocapsid in cytoplasm. We provide direct microscopic evidence of Polypyrimidine tract binding protein (PTB) mediated inhibition of nuclear export of a pgRNA based intron-containing pre-mRNA (CPS-PRE) with quantitative RNA-FISH. We also demonstrate through RNA immunoprecipitation experiments that CPS-PRE minigene transcripts stably interact with members of NXF1-NXT1 pathway and no crosslinking with karyopherin CRM1 could be seen. Our data reinforces a novel aspect of PTB in pre-mRNA nuclear export for active retention of intron-containing transcripts and directly shows the ability of pgRNA components to interact with NXF1-NXT1 heterodimer. papers.full_text_excerpt: Abstract Hepatitis B virus, a pararetrovirus and member of hepadnaviridae family, harbours a partially double-stranded DNA genome that is transcribed by the host RNA polymerase II to generate an intron-containing pregenomic RNA (pgRNA). Nuclear export of pgRNA utilizing the canonical host pathways remains central to successful virus replication since it is reverse transcribed by the viral P protein within the nucleocapsid in cytoplasm. We provide direct microscopic evidence of Polypyrimidine tract binding protein (PTB) mediated inhibition of nuclear export of a pgRNA based intron-containing pre-mRNA (CPS-PRE) with quantitative RNA-FISH. We also demonstrate through RNA immunoprecipitation experiments that CPS-PRE minigene transcripts stably interact with members of NXF1-NXT1 pathway and no crosslinking with karyopherin CRM1 could be seen. papers.title_original: A Hepatitis B virus pregenomic RNA based minigene transcript utilizes polypyrimidine tract binding protein regulated NXF1-NXT1 nuclear export pathway

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication depends on nuclear export of its pregenomic RNA (pgRNA), yet the host pathways mediating export of intron-containing pgRNA transcripts remain incompletely defined. The study addresses a knowledge gap regarding how HBV pgRNA, which contains introns, accesses the host nuclear export machinery despite host mechanisms that typically retain unspliced transcripts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used cell culture models to examine nuclear export of a pgRNA-based minigene transcript (CPS-PRE) containing HBV post-transcriptional regulatory elements. The experimental system involved human-derived cells and employed RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (RNA-FISH) and RNA immunoprecipitation to visualize and quantify transcript localization and protein interactions.
analysis.methods: RNA-FISH was used to visualize the subcellular localization of CPS-PRE minigene transcripts, and RNA immunoprecipitation assays were performed to assess interactions between these transcripts and host nuclear export factors, specifically members of the NXF1-NXT1 pathway. Polypyrimidine tract-binding protein (PTB) was evaluated for its role in modulating nuclear export of the intron-containing transcripts.
analysis.main_results: Microscopy showed that PTB inhibits nuclear export of the intron-containing CPS-PRE minigene transcript, resulting in its nuclear retention. RNA immunoprecipitation demonstrated stable interaction of CPS-PRE transcripts with the NXF1-NXT1 export machinery, while no interaction was detected with the karyopherin CRM1 pathway.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a novel regulatory mechanism in which PTB actively retains intron-containing pgRNA-derived transcripts in the nucleus, counteracting the NXF1-NXT1 mediated export pathway. This demonstrates that HBV pgRNA components can engage the host NXF1-NXT1 export system despite the presence of introns, challenging the assumption that unspliced viral RNAs are excluded from this pathway.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies PTB and the NXF1-NXT1 pathway as potential targets for therapeutic intervention to disrupt HBV replication by impairing pgRNA nuclear export. These insights may inform strategies to modulate host-virus interactions and improve antiviral approaches against chronic HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro cell culture models and does not evaluate the mechanism in primary human hepatocytes or in vivo. While the evidence strongly supports PTB-mediated nuclear retention and NXF1-NXT1 interaction, the generalizability to natural HBV infection and the impact on viral replication require further validation in physiologically relevant systems.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Hepatitis B virus (HBV) pregenomic RNA (pgRNA), which contains introns, accesses host nuclear export pathways despite cellular mechanisms that typically retain unspliced transcripts. Using cell culture models, the authors demonstrate that a pgRNA-based minigene transcript (CPS-PRE) interacts with the NXF1-NXT1 nuclear export machinery but is actively retained in the nucleus by the host protein PTB, as shown by RNA-FISH and RNA immunoprecipitation. The findings reveal a novel regulatory role for PTB in restricting nuclear export of intron-containing pgRNA-derived transcripts and highlight the NXF1-NXT1 pathway as a potential antiviral target. However, the study is limited to in vitro systems and requires validation in primary human hepatocytes or in vivo models to confirm its relevance to natural HBV infection and replication.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 复制依赖于其前基因组 RNA (pgRNA) 的核输出,但介导含内含子 pgRNA 转录物输出的 宿主 途径仍未完全确定。该研究解决了关于包含内含子的 HBV pgRNA 如何访问 宿主 核输出机制的知识差距,尽管 宿主 机制通常保留未剪接的转录本。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用细胞培养模型来检查含有 HBV 转录后调控元件的基于 pgRNA 的小基因转录本 (CPS-PRE) 的核输出。该实验系统涉及人源细胞,并采用 RNA 荧光原位杂交 (RNA-FISH) 和 RNA 免疫沉淀来可视化和量化转录本定位和蛋白质相互作用。
elements_zh.methods: RNA-FISH 用于可视化 CPS-PRE 小基因转录本的亚细胞定位,并进行 RNA 免疫沉淀测定来评估这些转录本与 宿主 核输出因子(特别是 NXF1-NXT1 通路成员)之间的相互作用。评估了聚嘧啶束结合蛋白(PTB)在调节含内含子转录本的核输出中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 显微镜检查显示,PTB 抑制含有内含子的 CPS-PRE 小基因转录本的核输出,导致其核保留。RNA 免疫沉淀证明 CPS-PRE 转录本与 NXF1-NXT1 输出机制存在稳定的相互作用,而未检测到与核转运蛋白 CRM1 途径的相互作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现揭示了一种新的调节机制,其中 PTB 主动将含有内含子的 pgRNA 衍生转录物保留在细胞核中,抵消 NXF1-NXT1 介导的输出途径。这表明,尽管存在内含子,但 HBV pgRNA 成分仍可以参与 宿主 NXF1-NXT1 输出系统,挑战了未剪接的病毒 RNA 被排除在该途径之外的假设。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究将 PTB 和 NXF1-NXT1 通路确定为治疗干预的潜在目标,通过损害 pgRNA 核输出来破坏 HBV 复制。这些见解可能会为调节 宿主 病毒相互作用的策略提供信息,并改进 抗病毒药物 对抗慢性 HBV 感染的方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外细胞培养模型,并未评估原代人肝细胞或体内的机制。虽然证据强烈支持 PTB 介导的核滞留和 NXF1-NXT1 相互作用,但自然 HBV 感染的普遍性以及对病毒复制的影响需要在生理相关系统中进一步验证。

analysis_zh.methods: RNA-FISH 用于可视化 CPS-PRE 小基因转录本的亚细胞定位,并进行 RNA 免疫沉淀测定来评估这些转录本与 宿主 核输出因子(特别是 NXF1-NXT1 通路成员)之间的相互作用。评估了聚嘧啶束结合蛋白(PTB)在调节含内含子转录本的核输出中的作用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 显微镜检查显示,PTB 抑制含有内含子的 CPS-PRE 小基因转录本的核输出,导致其核保留。RNA 免疫沉淀证明 CPS-PRE 转录本与 NXF1-NXT1 输出机制存在稳定的相互作用,而未检测到与核转运蛋白 CRM1 途径的相互作用。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现揭示了一种新的调节机制,其中 PTB 主动将含有内含子的 pgRNA 衍生转录物保留在细胞核中,抵消 NXF1-NXT1 介导的输出途径。这表明,尽管存在内含子,但 HBV pgRNA 成分仍可以参与 宿主 NXF1-NXT1 输出系统,挑战了未剪接的病毒 RNA 被排除在该途径之外的假设。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究将 PTB 和 NXF1-NXT1 通路确定为治疗干预的潜在目标,通过损害 pgRNA 核输出来破坏 HBV 复制。这些见解可能会为调节 宿主 病毒相互作用的策略提供信息,并改进 抗病毒药物 对抗慢性 HBV 感染的方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外细胞培养模型,并未评估原代人肝细胞或体内的机制。虽然证据强烈支持 PTB 介导的核滞留和 NXF1-NXT1 相互作用,但自然 HBV 感染的普遍性以及对病毒复制的影响需要在生理相关系统中进一步验证。

papers.title: Risk factors for low-level viremia in tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-treated chronic hepatitis B patients with advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated cirrhosis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Patients diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) complicated by advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated cirrhosis face a significant risk of disease progression. Despite first-line nucleos(t)ide analog therapy, some patients continues to exhibit low-level viremia (LLV). Furthermore, LLV is closely associated with accelerated liver fibrosis progression and a higher likelihood of hepatocellular carcinoma. Clinical studies on accurate prognostic indicators for LLV in this patient group are still comparatively rare. AIM To identify the high-risk factors linked to the occurrence of LLV among CHB patients with advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective study enrolled 141 CHB patients with advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated cirrhosis who received tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF). Patients were allocated into two groups according to their virological response at week 48 after treatment initiation: LLV, defined as hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels of 20-2000 IU/mL, and complete virological response (CVR), defined as HBV DNA levels below 20 IU/mL. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis were carried out to determine risk factors for LLV development. RESULTS A total of 141 patients were included in this study, among whom 17.0% (24/141) developed LLV. Significant differences were identified between the LLV and CVR groups regarding baseline HBV DNA, HBV RNA, hepatitis B e antigen positivity, HBV DNA ≥ 5.0 Log10 IU/mL, 6.0 Log10 IU/mL, 7.0 Log10 IU/mL, HBV RNA ≥ 5.0 Log10 copies/mL, and baseline alpha-fetoprotein. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that that HBV DNA ≥ 7.0 Log10 IU/mL (OR = 18.824, 95%CI: 1.608-220.404, P = 0.019) at baseline was associated with the occurrence of LLV. CONCLUSION In TDF-treated CHB with advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated liver cirrhosis, HBV DNA ≥ 7.0 Log10 IU/mL is a high-risk factor associated with LLV.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为患有晚期纤维化的 CHB 患者的临床监测策略提供信息,从而可以对 LLV 及其相关并发症(如加速肝纤维化进展和肝细胞癌)风险较高的患者进行早期干预。

papers.title: Multi-Mechanistic Treatment Approaches for Hepatitis B and Malaria
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B (HBV) and malaria are highest global challenges for infectious diseases. Both are substantial global health and socioeconomic challenges for higher risks of disease and early death. Cure and therapies are absent and limited. Prolonged treatment regimens are mandated with common suboptimal patient adherence and drug resistance. All underscore the need for newer therapeutic approaches that can achieve durable pathogen control. To this end, we examined the feasibility of combinatorial long-acting (LA) therapeutic approaches to improve the treatment outcomes of chronic HBV (CHB) infection which remains a major risk factor for progressive cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although available nucleos(t)ide analog therapies effectively suppress viral replication, they require long-term daily administration. We employed a three-pronged therapeutic strategy using LA prodrug formulations of tenofovir (TFV), a potent nucleos(t)ide analog, and tizoxanide (TIZ), an innate immune enhancer, to sustain viral suppression and improve immune homeostasis. We co-administered LA medicines (termed M5TFV and M2TIZ) in a CHB mouse model. The resulting multi-mechanistic strategy provided sustained antiviral suppression and reduced inflammation and fibrosis. An added part of the dissertation focused on improving limitations in bioavailability, half-life, resistance, and efficacy for existing malaria therapies.

papers.title_zh: 治疗乙型肝炎和疟疾的多机制 治疗 方法
papers.source_body_en: Hepatitis B (HBV) and malaria are highest global challenges for infectious diseases. Both are substantial global health and socioeconomic challenges for higher risks of disease and early death. Cure and therapies are absent and limited. Prolonged treatment regimens are mandated with common suboptimal patient adherence and drug resistance. All underscore the need for newer therapeutic approaches that can achieve durable pathogen control. To this end, we examined the feasibility of combinatorial long-acting (LA) therapeutic approaches to improve the treatment outcomes of chronic HBV (CHB) infection which remains a major risk factor for progressive cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although available nucleos(t)ide analog therapies effectively suppress viral replication, they require long-term daily administration. We employed a three-pronged therapeutic strategy using LA prodrug formulations of tenofovir (TFV), a potent nucleos(t)ide analog, and tizoxanide (TIZ), an innate immune enhancer, to sustain viral suppression and improve immune homeostasis. We co-administered LA medicines (termed M5TFV and M2TIZ) in a CHB mouse model. The resulting multi-mechanistic strategy provided sustained antiviral suppression and reduced inflammation and fibrosis. An added part of the dissertation focused on improving limitations in bioavailability, half-life, resistance, and efficacy for existing malaria therapies.
papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎 (HBV) 和疟疾是全球传染病面临的最大挑战。两者都是全球健康和社会经济面临的重大挑战,导致疾病和过早死亡的风险更高。治愈和疗法不存在且有限。延长 治疗 方案通常会导致患者依从性不佳和耐药。所有这些都强调需要能够实现持久病原体控制的新治疗方法。为此,我们研究了组合长效(LA)治疗方法来改善慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)感染的治疗结果的可行性,慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)感染仍然是进行性肝硬化和肝细胞癌的主要危险因素。尽管现有的核苷(酸)类似物疗法可以有效抑制病毒复制,但它们需要长期每日给药。我们采用了三管齐下的治疗策略,使用替诺福韦(TFV)(一种有效的核苷(酸)类似物)和替唑尼特(TIZ)(一种先天免疫增强剂)的LA前药制剂,以维持病毒抑制并改善免疫稳态。我们在 CHB 小鼠模型中共同施用 LA 药物(称为 M5TFV 和 M2TIZ)。由此产生的多机制策略提供了持续的 抗病毒药物 抑制并减少炎症和纤维化。论文的另一部分重点是改善现有疟疾疗法在生物利用度、半衰期、耐药性和功效方面的局限性。

papers.title: Knowledge, Attitude and Preventive Practices Towards Hepatitis B Virus Prevention and Screening: A Community-Based Study in AMAC, Abuja, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) poses a significant public health challenge globally, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria. This study assessed the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) of residents in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC) regarding HBV prevention and screening. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 401 residents of AMAC. Participants were systematically selected from households in urban and rural areas. Data were collected using a structured, closed-ended questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics and KAP regarding HBV. Descriptive and inferential analyses were performed using SPSS version 25. Results: Of the respondents, 51.6% were female and 48.4% were male, with the majority (60.1%) residing in urban areas. The overall knowledge rate was 56.6%, with notable gaps in understanding HBV transmission and prevention. Attitude toward HBV prevention was predominantly positive (68.1%), with strong support for vaccination and healthy practices. The practice rate was 66.4%, indicating good adherence to preventive measures such as vaccination and avoidance of risky behaviors. Significant positive correlations were observed among knowledge, attitude, and practice levels (knowledge-attitude: r = .656, p < .01; attitude-practice: r = .616, p < .01). Factors significantly associated with higher KAP scores included education level, marital status, and age. Conclusion: The findings reveal gaps in HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Higher education and positive marital life experiences contribute to better awareness and proactive health behaviors. Public health interventions must address these disparities by promoting comprehensive education and tailored outreach to improve HBV prevention and screening outcomes.

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 预防和筛查的知识、态度和预防实践:尼日利亚阿布贾 AMAC 的社区研究
papers.source_body_en: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) poses a significant public health challenge globally, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria. This study assessed the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) of residents in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC) regarding HBV prevention and screening. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 401 residents of AMAC. Participants were systematically selected from households in urban and rural areas. Data were collected using a structured, closed-ended questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics and KAP regarding HBV. Descriptive and inferential analyses were performed using SPSS version 25. Results: Of the respondents, 51.6% were female and 48.4% were male, with the majority (60.1%) residing in urban areas. The overall knowledge rate was 56.6%, with notable gaps in understanding HBV transmission and prevention. Attitude toward HBV prevention was predominantly positive (68.1%), with strong support for vaccination and healthy practices. The practice rate was 66.4%, indicating good adherence to preventive measures such as vaccination and avoidance of risky behaviors. Significant positive correlations were observed among knowledge, attitude, and practice levels (knowledge-attitude: r = .656, p < .01; attitude-practice: r = .616, p < .01). Higher education and positive marital life experiences contribute to better awareness and proactive health behaviors. Public health interventions must address these disparities by promoting comprehensive education and tailored outreach to improve HBV prevention and screening outcomes.

papers.title: Metagenomic sequencing detects viruses and bacteria in a cross-sectional clinical cohort of undifferentiated febrile illness in Nigeria
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Molecular and microscopy-based diagnostic capacity is often insufficient or unavailable in places where infectious disease burdens are highest, such as in West Africa. Rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) can provide quick and affordable diagnoses of common infections but is an imperfect solution due to limitations around detecting and dealing with false-negative and false-positive results. An alternative to RDT is unbiased metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance. Here, we present data from unbiased metagenomic sequencing used to identify causes of undiagnosed febrile illness in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Proof of concept for this approach has been demonstrated by several groups who have identified epidemic and endemic viral diseases like Lassa fever, yellow fever, and chikungunya. We show that unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis can be used to identify RNA viruses in clinical samples. We sequenced RNA from sera of patients (n = 343), many of whom were acutely febrile (76%), in a survey of clinics in Jos. We detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11 %) specimens. Among these were hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most of the viruses identified are unlikely to cause clinical symptoms in the patients we sampled, their presence demonstrates the validity of our approach. Additionally, our sequencing data allowed us to identify genetic material from potentially pathogenic bacteria, another possible etiological agent of febrile illness. IMPORTANCE: In low-resource areas, fevers due to infectious pathogens are a major source of illness, but tools for detecting and identifying such pathogens are often limited. Unbiased approaches for identifying genetic material from all potentially infectious organisms in a sample represent an opportunity for discovering sources of fever. Metagenomic sequencing can improve insight into pathogen landscapes in low-resource settings, potentially providing early detection of disease outbreaks. However, unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) is no panacea; it is susceptible to contamination and false positives. We used mNGS to evaluate serum from >300 Nigerian clinic-goers in Jos, Nigeria, most of whom (>70%) had fevers of unknown origin. Our goal was to understand arbovirus prevalence in Jos, Nigeria, and identify the sources of infection not routinely monitored for at clinics. We detected hepatitis B virus, as well as nonpathogenic anelloviruses. Our study provides insight into the utility and limitations of mNGS for pathogen surveillance.

papers.abstract_original: UNLABELLED: Molecular and microscopy-based diagnostic capacity is often insufficient or unavailable in places where infectious disease burdens are highest, such as in West Africa. Rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) can provide quick and affordable diagnoses of common infections but is an imperfect solution due to limitations around detecting and dealing with false-negative and false-positive results. An alternative to RDT is unbiased metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance. Here, we present data from unbiased metagenomic sequencing used to identify causes of undiagnosed febrile illness in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Proof of concept for this approach has been demonstrated by several groups who have identified epidemic and endemic viral diseases like Lassa fever, yellow fever, and chikungunya. We show that unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis can be used to identify RNA viruses in clinical samples. We sequenced RNA from sera of patients (n = 343), many of whom were acutely febrile (76%), in a survey of clinics in Jos. We detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11 %) specimens. Among these were hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most of the viruses identified are unlikely to cause clinical symptoms in the patients we sampled, their presence demonstrates the validity of our approach. Additionally, our sequencing data allowed us to identify genetic material from potentially pathogenic bacteria, another possible etiological agent of febrile illness. IMPORTANCE: In low-resource areas, fevers due to infectious pathogens are a major source of illness, but tools for detecting and identifying such pathogens are often limited. Unbiased approaches for identifying genetic material from all potentially infectious organisms in a sample represent an opportunity for discovering sources of fever. Metagenomic sequencing can improve insight into pathogen landscapes in low-resource settings, potentially providing early detection of disease outbreaks. However, unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) is no panacea; it is susceptible to contamination and false positives. We used mNGS to evaluate serum from >300 Nigerian clinic-goers in Jos, Nigeria, most of whom (>70%) had fevers of unknown origin. Our goal was to understand arbovirus prevalence in Jos, Nigeria, and identify the sources of infection not routinely monitored for at clinics. We detected hepatitis B virus, as well as nonpathogenic anelloviruses. Our study provides insight into the utility and limitations of mNGS for pathogen surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of current diagnostic tools in low-resource settings by exploring the utility of metagenomic sequencing for identifying pathogens in febrile illness cases. The background highlights the insufficient diagnostic capacity in West Africa, where infectious fevers are prevalent but difficult to diagnose.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, involving 343 patients, many of whom had fevers of unknown origin. The study focused on clinical samples from these patients to evaluate the effectiveness of metagenomic sequencing in pathogen detection.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed unbiased metagenomic sequencing to analyze RNA from serum samples of patients. This approach allowed them to identify both viral and bacterial genetic material, including potential pathogens associated with febrile illness.
analysis.main_results: Five human-infecting viruses were detected in 11% of the specimens, including hepatitis B virus and several anelloviruses. The presence of these viruses, even if not causing symptoms, demonstrated the feasibility of the metagenomic sequencing approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides evidence that metagenomic sequencing can effectively identify pathogens in clinical samples, even in low-resource settings. This approach offers a new tool for understanding the pathogen landscape and detecting emerging diseases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that metagenomic sequencing can enhance pathogen surveillance and improve the identification of infectious causes of fever, which is critical for public health responses in regions with limited diagnostic resources.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the limitations of metagenomic sequencing, such as susceptibility to contamination and false positives, but presents a high-confidence approach for pathogen detection in clinical samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of metagenomic sequencing to identify pathogens in patients with undifferentiated febrile illness in Nigeria. The research highlights the limitations of traditional diagnostic methods in low-resource settings and demonstrates the potential of unbiased sequencing to detect both viral and bacterial agents. Five human-infecting viruses, including hepatitis B virus, were identified in 11% of the specimens, showcasing the feasibility of this approach. The study emphasizes the importance of metagenomic sequencing for improving pathogen surveillance and understanding the etiology of febrile illnesses. However, it also notes the challenges of contamination and false positives associated with this method. The findings suggest that this technique could be a valuable tool for identifying infectious causes of fever in resource-limited areas, contributing to better public health strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过探索宏基因组测序在发热性疾病病例中识别病原体的效用,解决当前诊断工具在资源匮乏环境中的局限性。这一背景凸显了西非的诊断能力不足,该地区感染性发热流行但诊断困难。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究在尼日利亚高原州乔斯进行,涉及 343 名患者,其中许多人出现不明原因发烧。该研究重点关注这些患者的临床样本,以评估宏基因组测序在病原体检测中的有效性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员采用无偏倚的宏基因组测序来分析患者血清样本中的 RNA。这种方法使他们能够识别病毒和细菌遗传物质,包括与发热性疾病相关的潜在病原体。
elements_zh.main_results: 11%的样本中检测到五种人类感染病毒,包括乙型肝炎病毒和几种指环病毒。这些病毒的存在,即使不会引起症状,也证明了宏基因组测序方法的可行性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供的证据表明,即使在资源匮乏的环境中,宏基因组测序也可以有效识别临床样本中的病原体。这种方法为了解病原体状况和检测新出现的疾病提供了一种新工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,宏基因组测序可以增强病原体 监测 的能力,并改善发烧感染原因的识别,这对于诊断资源有限的地区的公共卫生应对措施至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认宏基因组测序的局限性,例如易受污染和假阳性,但为临床样本中的病原体检测提供了一种高可信度的方法。

papers.title: Comparison of Factors Associated With 30-Day and 90-Day Readmission Among a Global Cohort of Patients Hospitalised With Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It remains unclear whether different factors influence 30- and 90-day readmission rates. We identified predictors of 90-day mortality in a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis. METHODS: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation (LT), and mortality were compared in prospectively enrolled, non-electively hospitalised adult patients with cirrhosis. RESULTS: We enrolled 4208 patients from 125 centres across 37 countries. Alcohol-related liver disease was the most common aetiology of cirrhosis (40%), followed by hepatitis B virus infection (21%); 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation (LT), and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. In multivariable analysis, country income was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission rates, the receipt of LT, and mortality within 30 and 90 days post-discharge (all p-values < 0.001). Independent predictors of higher rates of 30- and 90-day readmissions, respectively, were disease severity (p < 0.001, p = 0.003), prior ascites (p = 0.025, p = 0.016), prior hospitalisation (p < 0.001), hyponatremia (p < 0.001, p = 0.008), and in-hospital vasopressor use (p = 0.002, p = 0.011). Prior variceal bleeding independently predicted higher 90-day readmission rates, whereas age, disease severity, mechanical ventilation, and in-hospital vasopressor use (all, p < 0.001) increased odds of 30- and 90-day post-discharge death. Additionally, admission (p = 0.011) and nosocomial (p = 0.022) infections increased the odds of 90-day post-discharge death. CONCLUSION: In a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis, patients in high-income countries exhibited the highest rates of 30- and 90-day readmission, alongside lower mortality rates and a higher incidence of LT. Variables that predict 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission. Understanding these disparities is essential for achieving health equity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unresolved question of whether distinct clinical or demographic factors differentially influence 30-day versus 90-day hospital readmission among patients hospitalised with cirrhosis globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective, multicentre, non-elective cohort study enrolling 4208 adult patients with cirrhosis across 125 centres in 37 countries.
analysis.methods: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality were compared using multivariable analyses to identify independent predictors.
analysis.main_results: Among 4208 patients, 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation, and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. Country income level was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission, transplantation, and mortality (all p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that predictors of 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission, highlighting shared risk factors across time horizons and disparities linked to country income levels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted interventions addressing disease severity, prior ascites, hyponatremia, and infection control may reduce early and late readmissions, particularly in lower-income settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s abstract-only evidence limits detailed assessment of methodological rigor, potential biases, and generalisability beyond hospitalised cirrhosis populations, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This global prospective cohort study of 4208 hospitalised adults with cirrhosis identified shared predictors for 30- and 90-day readmission, including disease severity, prior ascites, prior hospitalisation, hyponatremia, and in-hospital vasopressor use. Country income level was significantly associated with readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality within both time frames. Alcohol-related liver disease accounted for 40% of cirrhosis aetiologies, and 47% of patients were readmitted within 90 days. The authors emphasise that variables predicting early readmission also predict later readmission, underscoring the need for equitable health strategies to address disparities linked to socioeconomic factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了一个尚未解决的问题,即不同的临床或人口因素是否对全球肝硬化住院患者的 30 天和 90 天再入院有不同的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性、多中心、非选择性 队列研究 研究,招募了 37 个国家 125 个中心的 4208 名成年肝硬化患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多变量分析比较与出院后 30 天和 90 天再入院、肝移植和 死亡率 相关的变量,以确定独立的预测因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在4208名患者中,47%再次入院,8%接受肝移植,23%在出院后90天内死亡。国家收入水平与 30 天和 90 天再入院、移植和 死亡率 显着相关(所有 p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,30 天再入院的预测因素也预测了 90 天再入院的情况,强调了不同时间范围内的共同风险因素以及与国家收入水平相关的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对疾病严重程度、既往腹水、低钠血症和感染控制的针对性干预措施可能会减少早期和晚期再入院,特别是在低收入环境中。
