analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unresolved question of whether distinct clinical or demographic factors differentially influence 30-day versus 90-day hospital readmission among patients hospitalised with cirrhosis globally.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective, multicentre, non-elective cohort study enrolling 4208 adult patients with cirrhosis across 125 centres in 37 countries.
analysis_en.methods: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality were compared using multivariable analyses to identify independent predictors.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 4208 patients, 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation, and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. Country income level was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission, transplantation, and mortality (all p < 0.001).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that predictors of 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission, highlighting shared risk factors across time horizons and disparities linked to country income levels.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted interventions addressing disease severity, prior ascites, hyponatremia, and infection control may reduce early and late readmissions, particularly in lower-income settings.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s abstract-only evidence limits detailed assessment of methodological rigor, potential biases, and generalisability beyond hospitalised cirrhosis populations, warranting moderate confidence.

papers.title_zh: 全球肝硬化住院患者 队列研究 中与 30 天和 90 天再入院相关的因素比较。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It remains unclear whether different factors influence 30- and 90-day readmission rates. We identified predictors of 90-day mortality in a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis. METHODS: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation (LT), and mortality were compared in prospectively enrolled, non-electively hospitalised adult patients with cirrhosis. RESULTS: We enrolled 4208 patients from 125 centres across 37 countries. Alcohol-related liver disease was the most common aetiology of cirrhosis (40%), followed by hepatitis B virus infection (21%); 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation (LT), and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. In multivariable analysis, country income was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission rates, the receipt of LT, and mortality within 30 and 90 days post-discharge (all p-values < 0.001). Independent predictors of higher rates of 30- and 90-day readmissions, respectively, were disease severity (p < 0.001, p = 0.003), prior ascites (p = 0.025, p = 0.016), prior hospitalisation (p < 0.001), hyponatremia (p < 0.001, p = 0.008), and in-hospital vasopressor use (p = 0.002, p = 0.011). Prior variceal bleeding independently predicted higher 90-day readmission rates, whereas age, disease severity, mechanical ventilation, and in-hospital vasopressor use (all, p < 0.001) increased odds of 30- and 90-day post-discharge death. Additionally, admission (p = 0.011) and nosocomial (p = 0.022) infections increased the odds of 90-day post-discharge death. CONCLUSION: In a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis, patients in high-income countries exhibited the highest rates of 30- and 90-day readmission, alongside lower mortality rates and a higher incidence of LT. Variables that predict 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission. Understanding these disparities is essential for achieving health equity.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景和目的:尚不清楚不同因素是否影响 30 天和 90 天的再入院率。我们在肝硬化住院患者的全球 队列研究 中确定了 90 天 死亡率 的预测因子。方法:在前瞻性入组、非选择性住院的成年肝硬化患者中,比较与出院后 30 天和 90 天再入院、肝移植 (LT) 和 死亡率 相关的变量。结果:我们招募了来自 37 个国家 125 个中心的 4208 名患者。酒精相关性肝病是肝硬化最常见的病因(40%),其次是 乙型肝炎病毒 感染(21%);47% 的患者再次入院,8% 的患者接受肝移植 (LT),23% 的患者在出院后 90 天内死亡。在多变量分析中,国家收入与 30 天和 90 天的再入院率、LT 的接受情况以及出院后 30 和 90 天内的 死亡率 显着相关(所有 p 值 < 0.001)。30 天和 90 天再入院率较高的独立预测因素分别是疾病严重程度 (p < 0.001,p = 0.003)、既往腹水 (p = 0.025,p = 0.016)、既往住院情况 (p < 0.001)、低钠血症 (p < 0.001,p = 0.008) 和住院情况血管加压药的使用(p = 0.002,p = 0.011)。既往静脉曲张出血独立预测较高的 90 天再入院率,而年龄、疾病严重程度、机械通气和院内血管加压药的使用(全部,p < 0.001)增加出院后 30 天和 90 天的死亡几率。此外,入院感染 (p = 0.011) 和院内感染 (p = 0.022) 会增加出院后 90 天的死亡几率。结论:在全球肝硬化住院患者 队列研究 中,高收入国家患者的 30 天和 90 天再入院率最高,同时 死亡率 率较低,LT 发病率 较高。预测 30 天再入院的变量也预测 90 天再入院。了解这些差异对于实现健康公平至关重要。

papers.title: Lipid metabolism remodeling the immunological landscape of hepatocellular carcinoma: From mechanisms to therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global malignancy with high incidence and poor survival rates. Etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions have emerged as a unifying framework for deciphering hepatocarcinogenesis. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are the two predominant etiological drivers for HCC. Although immunotherapy serves as a cornerstone of HCC treatment, therapeutic response varies considerably across distinct etiologies. Accumulating evidence suggests that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, thereby accounting for the heterogeneous responses to immunotherapy. Therefore, deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk may provide new opportunities to improve therapeutic responses. In this review, we propose the framework of etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions by comparing two major etiologies, HBV and MASLD. Moreover, taking into account the crucial role of lipid metabolism in hepatocarcinogenesis, dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies have also been included so as to offer potential therapeutic strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection within the context of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), focusing on HBV as a predominant etiological driver and its role in disease pathogenesis and therapeutic response variability.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review adopts a narrative framework comparing HBV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to explore etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions, integrating dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies as potential therapeutic strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV is identified as one of the two predominant etiological drivers of HCC, with accumulating evidence indicating that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, contributing to heterogeneous immunotherapy responses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved heterogeneity in immunotherapy responses across distinct etiologies, including HBV-associated HCC, without providing pooled estimates or definitive mechanistic explanations for these variations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk, particularly in HBV-associated HCC, is proposed as a priority to improve therapeutic responses, with dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies suggested as potential strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review frames hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) within an etiology-driven metabolic-immune interaction framework, identifying hepatitis B virus (HBV) as a key driver alongside metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). It synthesizes evidence that HBV-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism contributes to immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, which may underlie the variable responses to immunotherapy observed in HBV-associated HCC. The review emphasizes the need to decode these interactions to refine therapeutic strategies, proposing dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies as potential avenues. While HBV is highlighted as a predominant etiological factor, the review underscores unresolved heterogeneity in treatment responses and the lack of pooled mechanistic insights, signaling critical gaps for future research.

papers.title_zh: 脂质代谢重塑肝细胞癌的免疫景观:从机制到治疗。
papers.source_body_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global malignancy with high incidence and poor survival rates. Etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions have emerged as a unifying framework for deciphering hepatocarcinogenesis. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are the two predominant etiological drivers for HCC. Although immunotherapy serves as a cornerstone of HCC treatment, therapeutic response varies considerably across distinct etiologies. Accumulating evidence suggests that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, thereby accounting for the heterogeneous responses to immunotherapy. Therefore, deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk may provide new opportunities to improve therapeutic responses. In this review, we propose the framework of etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions by comparing two major etiologies, HBV and MASLD. Moreover, taking into account the crucial role of lipid metabolism in hepatocarcinogenesis, dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies have also been included so as to offer potential therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 肝细胞癌(HCC)仍然是全球主要的恶性肿瘤,具有高 发病率 和低生存率。病因驱动的代谢-免疫相互作用已成为破译肝癌发生的统一框架。乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和代谢功能障碍相关的脂肪肝病 (MASLD) 是 HCC 的两个主要病因驱动因素。尽管免疫疗法是 HCC 治疗 的基石,但不同病因的治疗反应差异很大。越来越多的证据表明,脂质代谢的病因特异性失调会导致肿瘤微环境中的免疫失衡,从而解释对免疫治疗的异质反应。因此,破译病因驱动的代谢免疫串扰可能为改善治疗反应提供新的机会。在这篇综述中,我们通过比较两种主要病因(HBV 和 MASLD),提出了病因驱动的代谢-免疫相互作用的框架。此外,考虑到脂质代谢在肝癌发生中的关键作用,饮食干预和脂质代谢靶向治疗也被纳入其中,以提供潜在的治疗策略。

papers.title: Oncoviruses at the Crossroads of Ageing and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms and Key Signalling Pathways.
papers.abstract: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The scope examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and its disease manifestations, including chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis. The central question addresses how HBV intersects with host cellular pathways linked to ageing and cancer, focusing on shared molecular mechanisms and signalling networks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that integrates current knowledge on oncoviruses, ageing, and cancer without specifying databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or selection methods. It does not report an included-study count, meta-analysis, or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HBV, alongside other oncoviruses, actively reprograms host signalling pathways such as p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions contribute to both tumourigenesis and ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, including immunosenescence and inflammaging.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not provide target-specific evidence on HBV genotypes or detailed mechanistic studies linking HBV to ageing pathways. It lacks discussion of heterogeneity across HBV genotypes, populations, or regions, and does not address unresolved mechanisms specific to HBV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need to elucidate HBV-specific mechanisms that bridge ageing and cancer to identify novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating HBV-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and its disease outcomes, including chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis. It explores how HBV intersects with host cellular pathways linked to ageing and cancer, focusing on shared mechanisms such as genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. The review concludes that HBV reprograms key signalling pathways (p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, Wnt/β-catenin), driving dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence, while also contributing to immunosenescence and inflammaging. However, the review lacks target-specific evidence on HBV genotypes, mechanistic heterogeneity, or unresolved mechanisms, and does not provide detailed implications for surveillance, diagnosis, or treatment specific to HBV.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该范围检查人类 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染及其疾病表现,包括 慢性乙型肝炎、急性乙型肝炎、HBV 相关肝细胞癌和 HBV 相关肝硬化。核心问题涉及 HBV 如何与与衰老和癌症相关的 宿主 细胞通路交叉,重点关注共享的分子机制和信号网络。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一种叙述性综合,整合了有关肿瘤病毒、衰老和癌症的当前知识,没有指定数据库、搜索日期、资格标准或选择方法。它不报告纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,HBV 与其他肿瘤病毒一样,主动重新编程 宿主 信号通路,例如 p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-连环蛋白,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用会导致肿瘤发生和衰老相关的细胞功能障碍,包括免疫衰老和炎症。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有提供有关 HBV 基因型的特定目标证据,也没有提供将 HBV 与衰老途径联系起来的详细机制研究。它缺乏对 HBV 基因型、人群或地区异质性的讨论,也没有解决 HBV 特有的未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要阐明连接衰老和癌症的 HBV 特异性机制,以确定预防和治疗老龄化人群中 HBV 相关恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该范围检查人类 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染及其疾病表现,包括 慢性乙型肝炎、急性乙型肝炎、HBV 相关肝细胞癌和 HBV 相关肝硬化。核心问题涉及 HBV 如何与与衰老和癌症相关的 宿主 细胞通路交叉,重点关注共享的分子机制和信号网络。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一种叙述性综合,整合了有关肿瘤病毒、衰老和癌症的当前知识,没有指定数据库、搜索日期、资格标准或选择方法。它不报告纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,HBV 与其他肿瘤病毒一样,主动重新编程 宿主 信号通路,例如 p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-连环蛋白,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用会导致肿瘤发生和衰老相关的细胞功能障碍,包括免疫衰老和炎症。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有提供有关 HBV 基因型的特定目标证据,也没有提供将 HBV 与衰老途径联系起来的详细机制研究。它缺乏对 HBV 基因型、人群或地区异质性的讨论,也没有解决 HBV 特有的未解决的机制。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要阐明连接衰老和癌症的 HBV 特异性机制,以确定预防和治疗老龄化人群中 HBV 相关恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。

papers.title: Stimulation of the STING pathway leads to inhibition of HBV replication: insights into the role of hepatic macrophages.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Activation of the host immune system is a promising strategy for treating hepatitis B (HBV). The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway acts as an innate immune sensor for viral DNA. We aimed to determine whether STING activation can inhibit HBV replication in the liver. Methods We evaluated STING expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and liver biopsy specimens from patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). We examined the effect of the STING agonist DMXAA on HBV replication and the immune response in a mouse model with persistent HBV replication (rAAV8-HBV1.3). Additionally, we depleted macrophages in vivo to assess their role in DMXAA’s antiviral effects. Results STING expression in CHB patients was higher in the immune-active phase than in the inactive phase or uninfected healthy controls, suggesting an association between elevated STING expression and immune activation. In a mouse model with persistent HBV replication, DMXAA reduced serum HBV DNA in a dose-dependent manner, whereas repeated administration reduced serum HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels and enhanced hepatic immune responses. Transcriptome sequencing of liver tissues revealed 856 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in immune-related signaling pathways. In hepatic macrophage-depleted mice, the reductions in HBV virological markers following DMXAA treatment were less pronounced. Conclusions STING pathway activation enhances the immune response against HBV by upregulating the expression of immune-related genes. Hepatic macrophages play an important role in STING-mediated inhibition of HBV replication.

It explores the role of hepatic macrophages in this process by examining STING expression in CHB patients and testing the effects of the STING agonist DMXAA in a mouse model. The evidence is based on transcriptome sequencing and in vivo experiments, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title_zh: 刺激 STING 通路可抑制 HBV 复制:深入了解肝巨噬细胞的作用。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Activation of the host immune system is a promising strategy for treating hepatitis B (HBV). The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway acts as an innate immune sensor for viral DNA. We aimed to determine whether STING activation can inhibit HBV replication in the liver. Methods We evaluated STING expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and liver biopsy specimens from patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). We examined the effect of the STING agonist DMXAA on HBV replication and the immune response in a mouse model with persistent HBV replication (rAAV8-HBV1.3). Additionally, we depleted macrophages in vivo to assess their role in DMXAA’s antiviral effects. Results STING expression in CHB patients was higher in the immune-active phase than in the inactive phase or uninfected healthy controls, suggesting an association between elevated STING expression and immune activation. In a mouse model with persistent HBV replication, DMXAA reduced serum HBV DNA in a dose-dependent manner, whereas repeated administration reduced serum HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels and enhanced hepatic immune responses. Transcriptome sequencing of liver tissues revealed 856 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in immune-related signaling pathways. In hepatic macrophage-depleted mice, the reductions in HBV virological markers following DMXAA treatment were less pronounced. Conclusions STING pathway activation enhances the immune response against HBV by upregulating the expression of immune-related genes. Hepatic macrophages play an important role in STING-mediated inhibition of HBV replication.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 激活 宿主 免疫系统是治疗乙型肝炎 (HBV) 的一种有前景的策略。干扰素基因刺激剂 (STING) 信号通路充当病毒 DNA 的先天免疫传感器。我们的目的是确定 STING 激活是否可以抑制肝脏中的 HBV 复制。方法 我们评估了 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者外周血单核细胞 (PBMC) 和肝活检标本中 STING 的表达。我们在具有持续 HBV 复制的小鼠模型 (rAAV8-HBV1.3) 中检查了 STING 激动剂 DMXAA 对 HBV 复制和 免疫应答 的影响。此外,我们还耗尽了体内巨噬细胞,以评估它们在 DMXAA 的 抗病毒药物 效应中的作用。结果 CHB 患者的 STING 表达在免疫活跃期高于非活跃期或未感染的健康对照,表明 STING 表达升高与免疫激活之间存在关联。在持续 HBV 复制的小鼠模型中,DMXAA 以剂量依赖性方式降低血清 HBV DNA,而重复给药则降低血清 HBV DNA、HBsAg 和 HBeAg 水平,并增强肝脏 免疫应答。肝组织的转录组测序揭示了涉及免疫相关信号通路的 856 个差异表达基因 (DEG)。在肝巨噬细胞耗尽的小鼠中,DMXAA 治疗 后 HBV 病毒学标志物的降低不太明显。结论 STING 通路激活通过上调免疫相关基因的表达增强 免疫应答 抗 HBV 的能力。肝巨噬细胞在 STING 介导的 HBV 复制抑制中发挥重要作用。

papers.title: HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels at year 6 do not predict HCC risk in patients with cirrhosis on long-term entecavir therapy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prognostic value of on-treatment hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA, hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg), and quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains uncertain. We evaluate the predictive roles of these viral markers in patients with CHB receiving long-term entecavir therapy. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter study enrolled patients with CHB-related cirrhosis undergoing long-term entecavir treatment and HCC surveillance in Taiwan. Serum HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were measured at enrollment. Multivariable regression identified predictors of HBV RNA positivity and HCC development. RESULTS: Overall, 451 patients were included. After a median of 6.2 years of antiviral therapy, the median levels of HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg were 0.9 log10 copies/mL, 3.2 log10 U/mL, and 2.4 log10 IU/mL, respectively. During a median 3.3-year follow-up, 55 developed HCC. 57.2% of patients had detectable HBV RNA. HBV RNA detectability was associated with older age, lower alanine aminotransferase (ALT), HBeAg positivity, and higher HBsAg and HBcrAg levels. In multivariable analysis, higher fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [aSHR], 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.21) and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (aSHR, 1.01; 95% CI 1.00-1.01) independently predicted HCC development, whereas the three viral markers did not. CONCLUSION: After a 6-year entecavir therapy, 57.2% of patients with CHB-related cirrhosis had detectable HBV RNA. Year-6 HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were not predictive of HCC, while FIB-4 index and AFP remained independent predictors.

papers.title_zh: 第 6 年的 HBV RNA、HBcrAg 和 HBsAg 水平并不能预测长期接受恩替卡韦治疗的肝硬化患者的 HCC 风险。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prognostic value of on-treatment hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA, hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg), and quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains uncertain. We evaluate the predictive roles of these viral markers in patients with CHB receiving long-term entecavir therapy. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter study enrolled patients with CHB-related cirrhosis undergoing long-term entecavir treatment and HCC surveillance in Taiwan. Serum HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were measured at enrollment. Multivariable regression identified predictors of HBV RNA positivity and HCC development. RESULTS: Overall, 451 patients were included. After a median of 6.2 years of antiviral therapy, the median levels of HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg were 0.9 log10 copies/mL, 3.2 log10 U/mL, and 2.4 log10 IU/mL, respectively. During a median 3.3-year follow-up, 55 developed HCC. 57.2% of patients had detectable HBV RNA. HBV RNA detectability was associated with older age, lower alanine aminotransferase (ALT), HBeAg positivity, and higher HBsAg and HBcrAg levels. In multivariable analysis, higher fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [aSHR], 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.21) and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (aSHR, 1.01; 95% CI 1.00-1.01) independently predicted HCC development, whereas the three viral markers did not. CONCLUSION: After a 6-year entecavir therapy, 57.2% of patients with CHB-related cirrhosis had detectable HBV RNA. Year-6 HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were not predictive of HCC, while FIB-4 index and AFP remained independent predictors.

papers.title: Emerging Techniques of CRISPR/Cas System in Antiviral Therapy and Diagnostics: Applications, Limitations, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: The CRISPR/Cas (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) system is a versatile technology for developing antiviral medicines and editing viral genomes in both diagnostics and vaccine synthesis. Emerging insights into class 2 effectors, such as Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, which target viral DNA and RNA, have revolutionized vaccines against viruses such as HIV, HPV, HBV, and EBV. Innovative diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA have demonstrated system's diversity and accuracy in detecting the virus markers, supporting clinical decision-making, indicating adaptability and precision of CRISPR. This review critically evaluates CRISPR's role in RNA editing, emphasizing its importance for functional genomics and development of recombinant vaccines. Translational challenges are critically discussed, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical issues, for which unique approaches such as high-fidelity Cas variants, non-viral delivery systems, and bioethical frameworks are evaluated to address these limitations. This review also covers other social implications, such as accessibility and biosecurity risks, associated with CRISPR technologies Collectively, these advances underscore the transformative potential of CRISPR technologies in shaping next-generation antiviral diagnostics and therapeutics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the CRISPR/Cas system as a tool for antiviral therapy and diagnostics, with a focus on its potential applications against human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including its genotypes and associated diseases such as chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that evaluates class 2 CRISPR/Cas effectors (Cas9, Cas12, Cas13) and their roles in targeting viral DNA and RNA, with emphasis on HBV and other viruses such as HIV, HPV, HBV, and EBV. It discusses translational challenges including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical issues, but does not report systematic search methods, databases, eligibility criteria, or study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CRISPR/Cas systems, particularly Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, demonstrate versatility in antiviral applications, including genome editing and diagnostics. It highlights the adaptability and precision of CRISPR-based diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA for detecting viral markers, which support clinical decision-making.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies significant translational challenges, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical concerns, which remain unresolved. It also notes that while CRISPR systems show promise for HBV and other viral targets, the evidence base for HBV-specific applications is not systematically synthesized, and the long-term safety and efficacy in clinical settings are not established.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of high-fidelity Cas variants and non-viral delivery systems to mitigate off-target effects and improve delivery efficiency. It also emphasizes the need for bioethical frameworks to address ethical concerns and calls for further research to validate CRISPR-based diagnostics and therapeutics specifically for HBV in clinical practice.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the CRISPR/Cas system as a transformative tool for antiviral therapy and diagnostics, focusing on its potential against human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and associated diseases. It synthesizes evidence on class 2 CRISPR effectors (Cas9, Cas12, Cas13) and their roles in targeting viral DNA and RNA, highlighting their versatility in genome editing and diagnostics. Key diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA are noted for their adaptability and precision in detecting viral markers, supporting clinical decision-making. However, the review underscores unresolved translational challenges, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical concerns, which hinder clinical translation. It calls for the development of high-fidelity Cas variants, non-viral delivery systems, and bioethical frameworks to address these gaps. The evidence base for HBV-specific applications remains limited and unsystematically synthesized, emphasizing the need for further research to validate CRISPR-based interventions in clinical settings.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,CRISPR/Cas 系统,特别是 Cas9、Cas12 和 Cas13,在 抗病毒药物 应用中展示了多功能性,包括 基因组 编辑和诊断。它强调了基于 CRISPR 的诊断技术(例如 SHERLOCK、DETECTR 和 FELUDA)用于检测病毒标记物的适应性和精确性,从而支持临床决策。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了尚未解决的重大转化挑战,包括脱靶效应、交付限制和道德问题。它还指出,虽然 CRISPR 系统对 HBV 和其他病毒靶点显示出希望,但 HBV 特异性应用的证据基础尚未系统合成,并且临床环境中的长期安全性和有效性尚未确定。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑开发高保真 Cas 变体和非病毒递送系统,以减轻脱靶效应并提高递送效率。它还强调需要建立生物伦理框架来解决伦理问题,并呼吁进一步研究以在临床实践中验证基于 CRISPR 的 HBV 诊断和治疗方法。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the CRISPR/Cas system as a tool for antiviral therapy and diagnostics, with a focus on its potential applications against human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including its genotypes and associated diseases such as chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that evaluates class 2 CRISPR/Cas effectors (Cas9, Cas12, Cas13) and their roles in targeting viral DNA and RNA, with emphasis on HBV and other viruses such as HIV, HPV, HBV, and EBV. It discusses translational challenges including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical issues, but does not report systematic search methods, databases, eligibility criteria, or study counts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CRISPR/Cas systems, particularly Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, demonstrate versatility in antiviral applications, including genome editing and diagnostics. It highlights the adaptability and precision of CRISPR-based diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA for detecting viral markers, which support clinical decision-making.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies significant translational challenges, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical concerns, which remain unresolved. It also notes that while CRISPR systems show promise for HBV and other viral targets, the evidence base for HBV-specific applications is not systematically synthesized, and the long-term safety and efficacy in clinical settings are not established.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of high-fidelity Cas variants and non-viral delivery systems to mitigate off-target effects and improve delivery efficiency. It also emphasizes the need for bioethical frameworks to address ethical concerns and calls for further research to validate CRISPR-based diagnostics and therapeutics specifically for HBV in clinical practice.

papers.title_zh: 抗病毒药物 治疗和诊断中 CRISPR/Cas 系统的新兴技术:应用、局限性和转化视角。
papers.source_body_en: The CRISPR/Cas (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) system is a versatile technology for developing antiviral medicines and editing viral genomes in both diagnostics and vaccine synthesis. Emerging insights into class 2 effectors, such as Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, which target viral DNA and RNA, have revolutionized vaccines against viruses such as HIV, HPV, HBV, and EBV. Innovative diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA have demonstrated system's diversity and accuracy in detecting the virus markers, supporting clinical decision-making, indicating adaptability and precision of CRISPR. This review critically evaluates CRISPR's role in RNA editing, emphasizing its importance for functional genomics and development of recombinant vaccines. Translational challenges are critically discussed, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical issues, for which unique approaches such as high-fidelity Cas variants, non-viral delivery systems, and bioethical frameworks are evaluated to address these limitations. This review also covers other social implications, such as accessibility and biosecurity risks, associated with CRISPR technologies Collectively, these advances underscore the transformative potential of CRISPR technologies in shaping next-generation antiviral diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: Temporal Patterns of HBV Reactivation in Rituximab-Treated CKD Patients: An Exploratory Analysis of Baseline Quantitative HBsAg and Prophylaxis Duration.
papers.abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a severe complication in HBsAg-positive patients receiving rituximab (RTX) for chronic kidney disease (CKD). We evaluated clinical predictors of reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX. Participants were stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration: Group A (≥ 12-18 months post-RTX, n=41), Group B (6-12 months, n=47), and Group C ( Results The overall HBV reactivation was 7.6% (8/105). A significant "duration-dependent" protective effect was observed, with reactivation rates of 2.4%, 6.4%, and 23.5% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (P = 0.012). Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL (OR = 12.5, P = 0.005) and antiviral prophylaxis duration Conclusions An extended 12-18 months antiviral prophylaxis regimen provides optimal protection against HBV reactivation in CKD patients. Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL represents a noteworthy marker of heightened risk. Due to the limitations of a small event size, these findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Crucially, the observed temporal clustering between 4 and 10 months indicates a distinct post-prophylaxis risk timeline compared to non-renal populations, highlighting the need for further tailored, prospective validation.

We evaluated clinical predictors of reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX. Participants were stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration: Group A (≥ 12-18 months post-RTX, n=41), Group B (6-12 months, n=47), and Group C ( 2.4 log10 IU/mL (OR = 12.5, P = 0.005) and antiviral prophylaxis duration 2.4 log10 IU/mL represents a noteworthy marker of heightened risk. Due to the limitations of a small event size, these findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Crucially, the observed temporal clustering between 4 and 10 months indicates a distinct post-prophylaxis risk timeline compared to non-renal populations, highlighting the need for further tailored, prospective validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients receiving rituximab (RTX) are at risk of severe Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation, yet clinical predictors and optimal antiviral prophylaxis strategies remain uncertain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective analysis included 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX, stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration into three groups: Group A (≥12–18 months, n=41), Group B (6–12 months, n=47), and Group C (<6 months, n=17).
analysis.methods: The study evaluated clinical predictors of HBV reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics using retrospective data.
analysis.main_results: Overall HBV reactivation occurred in 7.6% (8/105) of patients, with reactivation rates of 2.4% in Group A, 6.4% in Group B, and 23.5% in Group C (P=0.012). Baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL was associated with increased risk (OR=12.5, P=0.005).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that extended 12–18 months of antiviral prophylaxis provides optimal protection against HBV reactivation in CKD patients, with baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL serving as a notable risk marker.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that prolonged antiviral prophylaxis may reduce HBV reactivation risk in RTX-treated CKD patients, particularly those with high baseline HBsAg levels, warranting prospective validation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s small event size and retrospective design limit causal inference and generalizability, and the authors classify the evidence as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory retrospective study analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients treated with rituximab (RTX) to identify predictors of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation and optimal antiviral prophylaxis duration. Patients were stratified by prophylaxis duration: ≥12–18 months (n=41), 6–12 months (n=47), and <6 months (n=17). Overall HBV reactivation occurred in 7.6% (8/105), with reactivation rates of 2.4%, 6.4%, and 23.5% across the three groups, respectively (P=0.012). Baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL was associated with increased risk (OR=12.5, P=0.005). The authors conclude that extended 12–18 months of prophylaxis provides optimal protection and that high baseline HBsAg levels identify patients at heightened risk. However, the small event size and retrospective design limit the strength of evidence, and the findings are exploratory.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 接受利妥昔单抗 (RTX) 治疗的慢性肾病 (CKD) 患者存在严重的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 再激活风险,但临床预测因子和最佳 抗病毒药物 预防策略仍不确定。

elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用回顾性数据评估了 HBV 再激活的临床预测因素、最佳预防持续时间和停药后风险动力学。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体 HBV 再激活发生率为 7.6% (8/105),其中 A 组再激活率为 2.4%,B 组为 6.4%,C 组为 23.5%(P=0.012)。基线 HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL 与风险增加相关(OR=12.5,P=0.005)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明延长 12-18 个月的 抗病毒药物 预防可以为 CKD 患者提供针对 HBV 再激活的最佳保护,基线 HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL 作为显着的风险标记。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些研究结果表明,长期 抗病毒药物 预防可能会降低接受 RTX 治疗的 CKD 患者的 HBV 再激活风险,特别是那些基线 HBsAg 水平较高的患者,值得前瞻性验证。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的小事件规模和回顾性设计限制了因果推理和普遍性,作者将证据分为探索性证据和假设生成证据。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 再激活是接受利妥昔单抗 (RTX) 治疗慢性肾脏病 (CKD) 的 HBsAg 阳性患者的严重并发症。我们评估了再激活的临床预测因素、最佳预防持续时间和停药后风险动力学。方法 我们回顾性分析了 105 例接受 RTX 治疗的 HBsAg 阳性 CKD 患者。根据 抗病毒药物 预防持续时间对参与者进行分层:A 组(RTX 后≥ 12-18 个月,n=41)、B 组(6-12 个月,n=47)和 C 组(结果 总体 HBV 再激活率为 7.6% (8/105)。观察到显着的“持续时间依赖性”保护作用,再激活率为 2.4%、6.4% 和A、B 和 C 组分别为 23.5%(P = 0.012)。基线 HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL(OR = 12.5,P = 0.005)和 抗病毒药物 预防持续时间 结论 延长 12-18 个月的 抗病毒药物 预防方案为 CKD 患者提供了针对基线 HBV 再激活的最佳保护。HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL 代表了风险升高的一个值得注意的标志。由于事件规模较小,这些发现仍然是探索性的和假设性的,至关重要的是,与非肾脏人群相比,观察到的 4 至 10 个月之间的时间聚类表明了不同的预防后风险时间线,这凸显了进一步定制的前瞻性验证的必要性。

papers.title: Seroprevalence and Early Indicators of HBV and HCV Co-infection Among Newly Diagnosed HIV Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study from India.
papers.abstract: HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections contribute significantly to liver-associated morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (HIV/AIDS). Detection of these hepatitis co-infections at the time of HIV diagnosis is critical for the selection of the most suitable HAART regimen to improve long-term health outcomes. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 newly diagnosed, HIV-1 adult patients and screened for HBV (HBsAg) and HCV (anti-HCV) using immunoassays. Sociodemographic, behavioral, hematological, biochemical, immunological, and virological parameters were analyzed. Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for co-infections. Among all participants HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections had 3.9% and 2.5% seroprevalence respectively. Previous or present injection drug use was the best predictor, with RRR = 74.86 (95% CI 11.7-478.9, p < 0.001) for HIV-HBV and RRR = 174.67 (95% CI 22.6-1348.1, p < 0.001) for HIV-HC Non-heterosexual HIV transmission modes were also significant predictors (RRR = 8.30, 95% CI 2.2-31.2, p = 0.002 for HIV-HBV; RRR = 10.9, 2.3-52.7, HCV, p = 0.003). Compared to HIV-only patients, co-infected patients had significantly elevated bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and ALP levels, lower platelet counts and serum albumin, higher ESR, and higher HIV viral loads. Furthermore, sexual orientation (< 0.001) and substance abuse (< 0.001) significantly contribute to health risk behaviors. These findings highlights the prevalence of HBV and HCV co-infection among newly diagnosed HIV patients is lower than the global prevalence among HIV/AIDS. However, the baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators of co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening in newly diagnosed HIV patients.

analysis.methods: Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for HBV and HCV co-infections among the participants.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from India assessed HBV and HCV co-infection among 282 newly diagnosed HIV-1 adult patients using immunoassays, finding seroprevalences of 3.9% for HIV-HBV and 2.5% for HIV-HCV. Injection drug use was the strongest predictor of co-infection (RRR 74.86 for HBV and 174.67 for HCV, p < 0.001), with co-infected patients showing elevated liver enzymes, lower platelet counts, and higher HIV viral loads. The authors conclude that baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators for HBV co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening at HIV diagnosis. The study acknowledges that HBV prevalence was lower than global estimates and notes limitations including the cross-sectional design and lack of genotype or long-term outcome data, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: HIV-HBV 合并感染对 HIV 感染者的肝脏相关发病率和 诊断 产生显着影响,而 HIV 诊断 的早期检测对于选择适当的抗逆转录病毒治疗以改善长期健康结果至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在印度 282 名新诊断的 HIV-1 成年患者中进行了一项横断面研究,这些患者使用免疫测定法筛查了 HBV (HBsAg) 和 HCV (抗 HCV),并分析了社会人口学、行为、血液学、生化、免疫学和病毒学参数。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多项逻辑回归来确定参与者中 HBV 和 HCV 合并感染的相对风险比 (RRR)。
elements_zh.main_results: HIV-HBV 和 HIV-HCV 合并感染的 血清流行率 分别为 3.9% 和 2.5%,之前或当前的注射吸毒被认为是最强的预测因子(HIV-HBV 的 RRR = 74.86,HIV-HCV 的 RRR = 174.67,均 p < 0.001)。与仅感染 HIV 的患者相比,合并感染的患者表现出显着升高的胆红素、SGOT、SGPT 和 ALP 水平、较低的血小板计数和血清白蛋白、较高的 ESR 和较高的 HIV 病毒载量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,基线实验室异常和高危行为可能作为 HBV 合并感染的早期指标,支持对新诊断的 HIV 患者进行常规肝炎筛查,并指出观察到的 HBV 合并感染 患病率 低于 HIV/AIDS 患者的全球估计值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在 HIV 诊断 进行常规 HBV 筛查可以及时做出治疗决策,特别是对于具有注射吸毒或非异性恋 传播 等高危行为的人群,以减轻肝病进展。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且该研究没有报告 HBV 基因型分布或长期临床结果,这将证据的普遍性和强度限制为中等。

news.title: Preventing Hepatitis B Vertical Transmission - Contagion Live
news.rss_summary_html: Preventing Hepatitis B Vertical Transmission  Contagion Live
news.excerpt_original: Preventing Hepatitis B Vertical Transmission Contagion Live
news.priority_tier_reason: 可信机构来源或已成功抓获正文
news.content: An estimated 172,000 infants acquired hepatitis B virus through mother-to-child transmission in the WHO African region in 2022, and combining birth-dose vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could cut this burden by more than 86%. Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR, discusses the barriers to eliminating vertical transmission of hepatitis B, and strategies to reduce the coverage gap. Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR Credit: UNC Hepatitis B virus continues to drive a heavy burden of chronic infection and early liver-related death among infants across the WHO African region, despite the availability of tools to prevent transmission at birth. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in Lancet Global Health estimated 172,000 cases of mother-to-child HBV transmission occurred in the region in 2022, accounting for 0.4% of all liveborn infants.1 Pooled HBsAg prevalence among pregnant individuals reached 6.2%, and 1 in 4 chronically infected infants will die prematurely from liver cancer or other liver-related complications.1 Raising timely birth-dose vaccination coverage to 90% could reduce vertical transmission by nearly 44%, and combining vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could lower transmission by more than 86%, though regional HepB-BD coverage remained at just 17% as of 2021.2 Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR, assistant professor of pediatric infectious diseases at UNC School of Medicine and a member of UNC's Institute for Global Health and Infectious Diseases, co-authored the analysis. In the following interview, Thompson discusses the barriers to eliminating vertical transmission of hepatitis B in the WHO African region and the investments needed to close the coverage gap. Contagion: Your analysis found that an estimated 172,000 cases of mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission occurred in the WHO African region in 2022. What do these findings tell us about the current burden of vertical transmission, and why has this route of infection remained such a significant challenge? Thompson: In collaboration with a group of esteemed hepatitis B experts and led by Drs. Nicholas Riches and Alexander Stockdale, I co-authored a systematic review and meta-analysis of vertical transmission of HBV in the WHO African region, which was published in Lancet Global Health in 2025. 1 An estimated 172,000 cases of vertical transmission occurred in the African region in 2022, representing 0.4% of all liveborn infants. These infants who are infected with HBV will develop lifelong chronic infection, and 1 in 4 of them will die an early death from liver cancer or other liver-related complications. The current state of HBV control in Africa is unacceptable and represents profound health inequity. Vertical transmission of HBV is entirely preventable by combining birth-dose vaccine for babies plus antiviral prophylaxis for pregnant people, but these strategies remain inaccessible in many low-resource settings. Birth-dose vaccine has been introduced in nearly two-thirds of African countries, but overall coverage remains low at 17% due to logistical challenges in vaccine administration within 24 hours of birth. Unfortunately, birth-dose vaccine is insufficient to interrupt vertical transmission in cases of high-risk HBV (maternal viral load ≥200,000 IU/mL and/or HBeAg positivity), when antiviral prophylaxis is recommended to reduce the viral load. Maternal antiviral prophylaxis is now recommended for all HBsAg+ pregnant women in low-resource settings where viral load testing is not available, but is rarely provided. Accessibility of these life-saving and cancer-preventing resources is paramount to eliminating vertical transmission in the WHO African region. Contagion: The study suggests that increasing hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination coverage to 90% could reduce vertical transmission by nearly 44%, while combining vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could reduce transmission by more than 86%. What are the biggest barriers to implementing these interventions across the region, and how can they be overcome? Thompson: The barriers to timely birth-dose vaccination are complex and exist on multiple levels: policy (eg insufficient advocacy and affordability), facility (eg lack of knowledge among healthcare personnel, stock-outs, and the short window for vaccine administration) and community (eg lack of knowledge among caregivers and insufficient community health worker (CHW) engagement). 3 Educational campaigns for providers and caregivers, CHW involvement, political and financial support, and innovative strategies to reach out-of-facility births are among the strategies that can improve birth-dose coverage. Strategies must be adapted to the local context to enhance implementation. Barriers to maternal antiviral prophylaxis are related to the novelty and cost of this approach. Prophylaxis for all HBsAg+ pregnant women in low-resource settings was recommended by the WHO beginning in 2024, and so many countries have yet to adopt this strategy. Cost of tenofovir therapy hinders widespread uptake. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, a one-month course of tenofovir costs $25-30, nearly half of the average monthly income. Integration into the existing HIV framework could defray cost and implementation challenges. Ongoing education efforts for providers and patients and subsidization of prophylactic tenofovir are also necessary to overcome implementation barriers. Contagion: You found that approximately 6.2% of pregnant women attending antenatal care were hepatitis B surface antigen-positive. How should these findings influence prenatal screening policies and maternal care practices in countries across sub-Saharan Africa? Thompson: Indeed, the pooled HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence was 6.2% among pregnant individuals in the WHO African region. Prenatal screening for HBV is the first step in the pathway towards elimination of vertical transmission, but is still not performed in many low-resource settings. Triple screening for HIV, HBV and syphilis should co-occur prenatally, and there are now many examples of success stories using this approach. 4 Contagion: The study concludes that eliminating mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission in the WHO African region is achievable with expanded vaccination and antiviral use. What policy changes or investments should governments and global health organizations prioritize now to reach the WHO elimination targets? Thompson: The gap between current HepB-BD coverage (18% in the African region) and the WHO goal for elimination at 90% coverage is substantial. However, bridging this gap is possible with dedicated political will and financial investment. One solution to overcoming this gap is Gavi’s catalytic funding that provides HepB-BD free of charge (usually $0.30 per dose), alongside country-level commitment to vaccine administration and implementation. HepB-BD needs to be coupled with maternal antiviral prophylaxis to truly reach elimination targets of <0.1% HBsAg prevalence among children <5 years old. Global health organizations and individual countries in the WHO African region must incorporate both HepB-BD and maternal antiviral prophylaxis as a packaged approach, including educational initiatives, CHW engagement, cost subsidization, and coupling of care with HIV and syphilis towards triple elimination. Elimination of vertical transmission of HBV is at our fingertips. We need to come together as a global community to make it a reality. news.content_original: An estimated 172,000 infants acquired hepatitis B virus through mother-to-child transmission in the WHO African region in 2022, and combining birth-dose vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could cut this burden by more than 86%. Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR, discusses the barriers to eliminating vertical transmission of hepatitis B, and strategies to reduce the coverage gap. Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR Credit: UNC Hepatitis B virus continues to drive a heavy burden of chronic infection and early liver-related death among infants across the WHO African region, despite the availability of tools to prevent transmission at birth. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in Lancet Global Health estimated 172,000 cases of mother-to-child HBV transmission occurred in the region in 2022, accounting for 0.4% of all liveborn infants.1 Pooled HBsAg prevalence among pregnant individuals reached 6.2%, and 1 in 4 chronically infected infants will die prematurely from liver cancer or other liver-related complications.1 Raising timely birth-dose vaccination coverage to 90% could reduce vertical transmission by nearly 44%, and combining vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could lower transmission by more than 86%, though regional HepB-BD coverage remained at just 17% as of 2021.2 Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR, assistant professor of pediatric infectious diseases at UNC School of Medicine and a member of UNC's Institute for Global Health and Infectious Diseases, co-authored the analysis. In the following interview, Thompson discusses the barriers to eliminating vertical transmission of hepatitis B in the WHO African region and the investments needed to close the coverage gap. Contagion: Your analysis found that an estimated 172,000 cases of mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission occurred in the WHO African region in 2022. What do these findings tell us about the current burden of vertical transmission, and why has this route of infection remained such a significant challenge? Thompson: In collaboration with a group of esteemed hepatitis B experts and led by Drs. Nicholas Riches and Alexander Stockdale, I co-authored a systematic review and meta-analysis of vertical transmission of HBV in the WHO African region, which was published in Lancet Global Health in 2025. 1 An estimated 172,000 cases of vertical transmission occurred in the African region in 2022, representing 0.4% of all liveborn infants. These infants who are infected with HBV will develop lifelong chronic infection, and 1 in 4 of them will die an early death from liver cancer or other liver-related complications. The current state of HBV control in Africa is unacceptable and represents profound health inequity. Vertical transmission of HBV is entirely preventable by combining birth-dose vaccine for babies plus antiviral prophylaxis for pregnant people, but these strategies remain inaccessible in many low-resource settings. Birth-dose vaccine has been introduced in nearly two-thirds of African countries, but overall coverage remains low at 17% due to logistical challenges in vaccine administration within 24 hours of birth. Unfortunately, birth-dose vaccine is insufficient to interrupt vertical transmission in cases of high-risk HBV (maternal viral load ≥200,000 IU/mL and/or HBeAg positivity), when antiviral prophylaxis is recommended to reduce the viral load. Maternal antiviral prophylaxis is now recommended for all HBsAg+ pregnant women in low-resource settings where viral load testing is not available, but is rarely provided. Accessibility of these life-saving and cancer-preventing resources is paramount to eliminating vertical transmission in the WHO African region. Contagion: The study suggests that increasing hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination coverage to 90% could reduce vertical transmission by nearly 44%, while combining vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could reduce transmission by more than 86%. What are the biggest barriers to implementing these interventions across the region, and how can they be overcome? Thompson: The barriers to timely birth-dose vaccination are complex and exist on multiple levels: policy (eg insufficient advocacy and affordability), facility (eg lack of knowledge among healthcare personnel, stock-outs, and the short window for vaccine administration) and community (eg lack of knowledge among caregivers and insufficient community health worker (CHW) engagement). 3 Educational campaigns for providers and caregivers, CHW involvement, political and financial support, and innovative strategies to reach out-of-facility births are among the strategies that can improve birth-dose coverage. Strategies must be adapted to the local context to enhance implementation. Barriers to maternal antiviral prophylaxis are related to the novelty and cost of this approach. Prophylaxis for all HBsAg+ pregnant women in low-resource settings was recommended by the WHO beginning in 2024, and so many countries have yet to adopt this strategy. Cost of tenofovir therapy hinders widespread uptake. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, a one-month course of tenofovir costs $25-30, nearly half of the average monthly income. Integration into the existing HIV framework could defray cost and implementation challenges. Ongoing education efforts for providers and patients and subsidization of prophylactic tenofovir are also necessary to overcome implementation barriers. Contagion: You found that approximately 6.2% of pregnant women attending antenatal care were hepatitis B surface antigen-positive. How should these findings influence prenatal screening policies and maternal care practices in countries across sub-Saharan Africa? Thompson: Indeed, the pooled HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence was 6.2% among pregnant individuals in the WHO African region. Prenatal screening for HBV is the first step in the pathway towards elimination of vertical transmission, but is still not performed in many low-resource settings. Triple screening for HIV, HBV and syphilis should co-occur prenatally, and there are now many examples of success stories using this approach. 4 Contagion: The study concludes that eliminating mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission in the WHO African region is achievable with expanded vaccination and antiviral use. What policy changes or investments should governments and global health organizations prioritize now to reach the WHO elimination targets? Thompson: The gap between current HepB-BD coverage (18% in the African region) and the WHO goal for elimination at 90% coverage is substantial. However, bridging this gap is possible with dedicated political will and financial investment. One solution to overcoming this gap is Gavi’s catalytic funding that provides HepB-BD free of charge (usually $0.30 per dose), alongside country-level commitment to vaccine administration and implementation. HepB-BD needs to be coupled with maternal antiviral prophylaxis to truly reach elimination targets of <0.1% HBsAg prevalence among children <5 years old. Global health organizations and individual countries in the WHO African region must incorporate both HepB-BD and maternal antiviral prophylaxis as a packaged approach, including educational initiatives, CHW engagement, cost subsidization, and coupling of care with HIV and syphilis towards triple elimination. Elimination of vertical transmission of HBV is at our fingertips. We need to come together as a global community to make it a reality. analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-08-09; Event date: 2022 (vertical transmission cases) and 2025 (meta-analysis publication).
analysis.location_and_population: WHO African region; pregnant individuals attending antenatal care; infants born in 2022.
analysis.event: A systematic review and meta-analysis published in Lancet Global Health in 2025, co-authored by Peyton Thompson, MD, MSCR, quantified the burden of mother-to-child hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission in the WHO African region and discussed strategies to eliminate vertical transmission.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 172,000 estimated cases of mother-to-child HBV transmission in 2022 (0.4% of liveborn infants); 6.2% pooled HBsAg prevalence among pregnant individuals; 1 in 4 chronically infected infants will die prematurely from liver cancer or liver-related complications; current HepB-BD vaccination coverage at 17% (2021); raising birth-dose vaccination to 90% could reduce transmission by nearly 44%, while combining vaccination with maternal antiviral prophylaxis could reduce transmission by more than 86%.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Vertical transmission is preventable via birth-dose vaccination and maternal antiviral prophylaxis; barriers include low HepB-BD coverage (17%), logistical challenges in vaccine administration within 24 hours of birth, lack of viral load testing, high cost of tenofovir prophylaxis ($25-30 per month in DRC), and limited provider education; WHO recommended maternal antiviral prophylaxis for HBsAg+ pregnant women in low-resource settings starting 2024; integration with HIV frameworks and subsidization of tenofovir are proposed solutions; prenatal triple screening (HIV, HBV, syphilis) is recommended but not universally implemented.

analysis.brief_en: A 2025 Lancet Global Health meta-analysis estimates 172,000 infants in the WHO African region acquired hepatitis B through mother-to-child transmission in 2022, with 6.2% of pregnant women HBsAg-positive. One in four chronically infected infants faces early death from liver cancer or complications. Current birth-dose vaccination coverage stands at just 17%, far below the 90% target needed to cut transmission by 44%. news.content: Latest Celebrity K-Pop Drama Movie Culture Latest Celebrity K-Pop Drama Movie Culture Home Culture As Hepatitis B Cases Decline, Liver Cancer Linked to Alcohol and Fatty Liver Is Rising. How Can It Be Prevented? By Jongho, Jang Published 2026-08-10 15:40 Share this article X Facebook Copy Copy URL copied. File photo courtesy of Unsplash [Sportschosun Reporter Jang Jong-ho] According to the 2023 cancer registry statistics, liver cancer was the seventh most common cancer in South Korea, but it had the second-highest mortality rate among cancer types. The five-year survival rate has improved significantly from 20.6% in 2001-2005 to 40.4% in 2019-2023, but it is still below the overall cancer average of 73.7%. Professor Immanuel of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery at Soonchunhyang University Bucheon Hospital explained, "Liver cancer is difficult to detect early because it usually causes no clear symptoms at first, and even when it has progressed significantly, it may only cause nonspecific symptoms such as indigestion, weight loss, loss of appetite, and fatigue. If liver function worsens, symptoms such as jaundice or ascites may also appear." ◇ The causes of liver cancer are shifting from viral hepatitis to fatty liver The main causes of liver cancer include chronic hepatitis B and C virus infections, cirrhosis, advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease, and alcohol-related liver disease. As vaccinations and antiviral treatments have become more widely used, the share of liver cancer caused by chronic hepatitis B has declined, while the share linked to alcohol-related liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease caused by obesity and diabetes has increased. With an aging population and changes in lifestyle, the number of fatty liver patients is rising, and this trend is expected to grow further. ◇ Personalized treatment should also take quality of life after treatment into account Liver cancer treatment is determined by a comprehensive assessment of not only the tumor's size and number, but also its location, whether major blood vessels are involved, liver function, the degree of cirrhosis, the patient's age, and overall condition. Treatment options include liver resection, liver transplantation, local therapies such as radiofrequency ablation, transarterial chemoembolization, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy. Liver resection and liver transplantation are representative curative treatments that can offer the possibility of a cure, but even for liver cancer at the same stage, it is important to tailor the treatment to the patient based on liver function, tumor location, and overall condition. Liver resection is planned by evaluating both the amount and function of the remaining liver after surgery, so that enough function is preserved even after part of the liver is removed. The decision to operate is made after comprehensively considering whether the tumor is near major blood vessels, whether it is multifocal, whether there is metastasis outside the liver, and the patient's overall condition. If liver function is severely impaired and the risk of postoperative liver failure is high, or if the tumor meets liver transplantation criteria and cirrhosis is advanced, liver transplantation may be considered instead of liver resection. ◇ Minimally invasive liver surgery and AI-based 3D imaging make procedures more accurate and safer Recent liver cancer surgery has rapidly evolved toward reducing incisions while improving surgical precision and safety. In the past, most liver cancer operations were performed as open surgery, but recently the use of minimally invasive liver surgery with laparoscopy and robots has expanded. Because minimally invasive surgery is performed through several small incisions, it has the advantages of less postoperative pain, a smaller wound burden, and faster recovery. Recently, its use has also expanded to donor liver surgery in living-donor liver transplantation. At medical institutions with extensive experience, laparoscopic and robotic donor liver resection is performed when appropriate after fully evaluating the donor's vascular and biliary structures, the volume of the remaining liver, and surgical risks. Advances in imaging technology have also played an important role in improving the precision and safety of minimally invasive surgery. Soonchunhyang University Bucheon Hospital reconstructs preoperative CT and MRI images into AI-based 3D imaging to analyze the positions of tumors, blood vessels, and bile ducts in three dimensions. This allows doctors to accurately understand each patient's anatomical structure and predict the extent of resection and the volume of the remaining liver, enabling safer and more precise surgical planning. ◇ Prevention through antiviral treatment, weight control, management of metabolic disease, and regular screening To prevent liver cancer, patients with chronic hepatitis B or C need antiviral treatment, proper weight management, reduced alcohol consumption, regular exercise, and control of blood sugar and dyslipidemia. However, antiviral treatment does not completely eliminate the risk of liver cancer. If cirrhosis is already present or liver damage has progressed, liver cancer can still develop after treatment. Therefore, high-risk groups such as patients with chronic hepatitis B or C, cirrhosis, or advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease need regular follow-up every six months, even if they have no special symptoms. Professor Immanuel said, "With recent major advances in treatment technology, the number of patients who can expect a cure when detected early is increasing, and a variety of treatment options are being developed that can deliver good outcomes even in advanced liver cancer." He added, "Because liver cancer usually does not cause special symptoms in its early stages, it is more important than anything else for high-risk individuals with liver cancer risk factors to undergo regular screening and detect it early, rather than waiting to visit the hospital after symptoms appear." He added, "Because liver cancer usually does not cause special symptoms in its early stages, it is more important than anything else for high-risk individuals with liver cancer risk factors to undergo regular screening and detect it early, rather than waiting to visit the hospital after symptoms appear." analysis.brief_en: South Korea is witnessing a significant epidemiological shift in liver cancer, with cases linked to hepatitis B virus (HBV) declining due to expanded vaccination and antiviral therapies, while alcohol-related and fatty liver disease-associated liver cancers are rising sharply. According to 2023 registry data, liver cancer remains the seventh most common cancer but has the second-highest mortality rate nationally. Five-year survival rates have improved to 40.4%, yet lag behind the overall cancer average. Experts attribute the trend to lifestyle changes and aging, with HBV now contributing less to new cases than metabolic and alcoholic liver disease. Prevention now focuses on antiviral treatment for chronic HBV/HCV, weight management, metabolic control, and regular six-month screening for high-risk groups. Treatment options have diversified, including minimally invasive surgery, AI-assisted 3D imaging, and advanced therapies such as immunotherapy and targeted treatments, offering better outcomes even in advanced stages.

Renew subscription Maybe later Subscribe for a month to get full access How undiagnosed Hepatitis B is driving liver cancer rates in Africa Sunday, August 09, 2026 In Africa, where roughly 64 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, the infection remains the leading cause of liver cancer. Photo credit: Shutterstock By Dr Chris Opio Associate professor and consultant gastroenterologist & hepatologist Aga Khan University Medical College and Aga Khan University Hospital What you need to know: With Africa accounting for nearly 68 percent of new global infections, Hepatitis B remains a hidden danger that can damage the liver for decades without symptoms. You may feel perfectly healthy and still be living with hepatitis B without knowing it. The virus can quietly damage your liver for years, with symptoms sometimes appearing only after serious complications have developed. Although hepatitis B is preventable, it remains a leading cause of liver cancer and premature death worldwide. Much of this suffering can be avoided through vaccination, a simple blood test, and effective treatment. Hepatitis B is caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV), one of five main viruses that cause hepatitis: A, B, C, D, and E. While some types cause only short-term illness, HBV can persist in the body for life. Over time, the chronic inflammation it triggers can scar the liver, potentially leading to cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most common type of primary liver cancer. Also read: I wasn't feeling sick, but I had Hepatitis B: The fight against a hiding virus The impact of hepatitis B is severe in Africa. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), around 240 million people globally were living with chronic hepatitis B in 2024, with roughly 64 million of them in Africa. That year, Africa accounted for nearly 68 percent of the estimated 900,000 new infections worldwide. Hepatitis B also caused about 1.1 million deaths, mostly from cirrhosis and liver cancer. Not everyone with chronic hepatitis B will develop cancer, but the link between HBV and liver cancer is among the strongest infection-cancer connections. The International Agency for Research on Cancer reported that hepatitis B caused about 380,000 cancer cases globally in 2020. In sub-Saharan Africa, hepatitis B remains the leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma. Exact figures vary by country, but studies indicate that HBV is responsible for about half of liver cancer cases in the region. In high-prevalence areas, particularly in West Africa, it is linked to 70 to 80 percent of liver cancers in younger adults. This is why liver cancer in Africa often strikes at a younger age than in other parts of the world. The virus spreads through infected blood and certain body fluids. In regions where it is common, transmission most often occurs from an infected mother to her baby during birth or through close contact in early childhood. It can also spread via unprotected sex, needle or syringe sharing, unsafe medical injections, contaminated tattoo or piercing equipment, occupational exposure to infected blood, or sharing sharp personal items like razors. However, hepatitis B does not spread through everyday contact. You cannot catch it by sharing food or water, using the same utensils, breastfeeding, hugging, holding hands, coughing, or sneezing. People living with hepatitis B should not face stigma or discrimination. One of the biggest challenges of hepatitis B is its silence. It often produces no symptoms for many years. Like HIV, a person can look and feel perfectly healthy while the virus quietly harms their liver. When symptoms do appear, they may include yellowing of the eyes or skin (jaundice), dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, joint pain, and flu-like symptoms. In rare cases, an acute infection can cause sudden, serious liver failure. Severe complications typically arise after decades of chronic infection. Advanced liver disease can cause a swollen abdomen due to fluid buildup (ascites), loss of appetite, weight loss, vomiting blood, confusion, malnutrition, kidney problems, cirrhosis, or liver failure. Waiting for these symptoms is risky, because advanced liver disease is much harder to treat. The best way to prevent serious complications is to detect the infection early. The only reliable way to know whether someone has hepatitis B is through a blood test. Symptoms alone cannot confirm the infection or distinguish it from other liver problems. Blood tests can show whether the infection is recent or chronic, whether a person has developed immunity after vaccination, or whether a previous infection has cleared. Additional tests can measure the amount of virus in the blood and assess the risk of disease progression and transmission. Doctors can also use tools like ultrasound, FibroScan, and other imaging scans to check whether the liver has developed significant scarring. Testing is especially important because many people do not know they are infected. In 2024, only about 65 million people, roughly 27 per cent of those with chronic hepatitis B worldwide, knew their status. Pregnant women should be tested, because identifying infection allows for interventions that can dramatically reduce transmission to newborns. Household contacts, sexual partners of infected individuals, healthcare workers, and people exposed to infected blood should also consider testing. Also read: Prevention and treatment of Hepatitis B Early treatment of hepatitis B can prevent liver cancer. Most people with uncomplicated acute hepatitis B do not require specific antiviral medicine, as many recover on their own. However, chronic hepatitis B can be managed effectively with oral antiviral drugs. This treatment reduces the risk of cirrhosis and lowers the likelihood of liver cancer. For many patients, treatment is long-term and may be lifelong. It is important to remember that antiviral treatment does not replace regular check-ups. People with chronic hepatitis B still have a risk of liver cancer, especially if they have cirrhosis or other risk factors, so they need ongoing medical care. Vaccination remains the best protection against hepatitis B. Every child should receive the first dose of the hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours, followed by the remaining doses according to the national immunization schedule. Children, teenagers, and adults who have not been vaccinated should also complete the full recommended series. Babies born to mothers with hepatitis B need urgent protection, and mothers with high viral levels may require antiviral treatment during pregnancy to reduce the risk of transmission. Completing the full hepatitis B vaccine series provides more than 95 percent protection. Being diagnosed with hepatitis B does not mean someone cannot live a normal, productive life. People with the infection can continue working, studying, and participating in family and community activities. They should maintain regular medical check-ups, eat a healthy diet, exercise regularly, avoid alcohol, and consult a doctor before using any herbal or over-the-counter medicines, since some products can harm the liver. They may also need testing for other viral hepatitis types, such as hepatitis C, and may require the hepatitis A vaccine if recommended. Hepatitis B can quietly damage the liver, but liver cancer from HBV does not have to happen. Vaccination can stop the infection. Testing can find those at risk. Treatment can slow the disease and save lives. The problem is not that we lack solutions. The real challenge is ensuring that people know their status and can access prevention and care. A simple vaccine, a blood test, and timely treatment can prevent lifelong liver disease.
